Now, I've played this game for nearly 2 hours when writing this review and it was the first time I have played, so let's get started with my first impressions and then follow through to a pros and cons section.
First Impressions:
So I first launched the game and found myself a launcher for it. I was a bit confused as I thought that the game would throw me right in. I hit the play button and nothing happened. "What?" I thought to myself as I quickly googled the problem and found no solution. I continued to attempt to "repair" and "redownload" the game from the launcher to no success. I then decided to check to see if the game was downloaded correctly from steam though the "Verify Game Cache" function in the games properties. I did this and found out that 7 files had not been downloaded. Withing 2-3 seconds I had those files and went back into the launcher of the game. It worked! I could download the game with no issues and finally got in.
Once the menu loaded I was blown away. The game, although in an early access stage, still had a very nice and sleek looking menu. The game looked and navigated quite professionally and is substantually better than some other early access games I have tried. After a bit of fiddling I managed to get the graphics to what my computer could run them at (max basically) and then decided to load up a world!
I was feeling a tab bit lazy so I decided to load up somebody else's creation. Very easy and simple to use navigation allowed me to load up somebody else's map that they had created. I could edit it, play on it, and even interact with it. From what I can see, nothing was missing from the user created map and everything was working just fine. From here on I got very excited. I wanted to make my own map. A map I could call home.
I loaded up a new map and got to work. After about an hour of learning the controls I had finally gotten a hang of it! I flew around adding blocks, destroying blocks, placing enemies, placing guns, and of course, placing jump pads. I finished a bit of my map with many jumping parkour areas and some more difficult jump pad areas to reach. Overall I got a fun map that I played on by myself for some time. I then decided that this wasn't enough. I needed a bit more of something "cool". I went into the menu to see what I could grab for myself and found hidden doors. Well, I used them as floors.
Once my map was finished I decided to see what else I could do with the game. The maps options were quite in depth with details such as: Gravity, Time of Day, Theme, and also Day/Night rotation being possible within the options. With my map done I decided to hop off the game and write a review, because overall the game amazed me. The graphics (although not spoken about much in this review, or even at all) are quite amazing and look very sleek. The character customization is fun and all of the weapons (although only a few so far) are perfect for an arena style shooter.
Now for the pros and cons:
Great graphics
Fun gameplay
Good progress in the games development
Easy sharing of your games
Has mutliplayer functionality (although I haven't explored it yet)
Has good plans for the future of it's development
Developer shows good knowledge of creating games
Can be played alone/Co-Op/Multiplayer/ in PvE or PvP
Many fun user created maps for the game
Relatively cheap to buy and well worth it!
It is only a 1 man developer team which worries me if he loses interest in developing the game.
The use of an independant launcher is cool, however steam updates would be a lot easier to keep track of from the users perspective.
No publically hosted games on official servers.

Hero of the Kingodm is a kind of ligthweight mix of point and click, resource management and treasure hunt but it's put together very neatly. At first I wasn't able to play the game due to some NVIDIA issues, but those were promptly resolved by the developer. He is very dedicated to making this game both in his vision and in the collective vision of the players.
Now onto the game!
At first glance, this game seems very polished already. The theme of a futuristic, "build your dream" platform works very well with the mechanics that have been established. Do you want to make a puzzle grid and challenge other players? Megatect can do that. Do you like sports or racing and want to invite your friends to play in your custom-built stadium? Megatect endorses that. Do you want to make an unforgiving deathmatch arena to stomp other players? MEGATECT ENCOURAGES IT!
The pros and cons of this game are really in favor of pros.
+ Graphics
+ Aesthetics
+ Environment
+ Music
+ Creativity
+ Infinite possibilities
- Underdeveloped (but it's Alpha)
- No mode selection preset for grids yet (i.e. "Deathmatch", "Race", etc.)
Other than that, I highly recommend dropping the money for this game as its potential is as limitless as your own creativity. Workshop grids will also be available in the near future, and the fact that the Dev plans on allowing you to host your own server with your friends and build your worlds together is amazing in of itself. I wholeheartedly endorse this game!

It should be horrible, but something about them just clicks with me.  I put in the 4-5 hours to finish the main story - there are a couple more achievements I could go after but I'm clicked out.  It's a step above hidden object games, and this one is much more sprawling than the first, meaning you'll be going back and forth a lot more, but even with that, I really enjoyed it.  It distills RPGs to their most basic traits and makes it work.

My review for this game is for my impression of the game after a few hours into the game.
This game plays sort of like the free to play game Air Mech. It has a main command unit which acts as a sort of "HERO" unit. Your entire game play is based on it. You unlock new units to spawn based on the level of your 'Commander' which means if you keep him in the back of your base, you wont be able to progress and win the game. This game has no passive money income so if you lose all your generation and cant afford to craft another income building youre dead. this game is sort of like a MOBA, where there are "lanes" and you have to defend your base while destroying theirs. The way this works is that you can create a building that automatically spawns a squad of 4 units to attack move to the enemy base.
The audio in the game's tutorials is all out of wack. There is no separation of channels into different volume levels. The in game sound effects and dialoge are the same volume so listening to the tutorial was frustrating. There is no custom key binding settings, and all the typcial settings you see in a normal game are gone from the menu as well.
Unit variations. There are, 2 Infantry units. There are 4 Ground Vehicles. There are 2 Air Units. There is also a Mega Unit which is a flying battleship that can launch a single fighter.
Units can be "Queued up" like in any other RTS game. Unfortunatly, this is not the case with crafting structures.
The way building works, is that there is a single power node which can link to 3 adjacent buildings, all buildings need power. you can only craft one building at a time, and you have to place them next to an active power node that has an available slot.
Ai pathing is pretty bad, and if youre fighting enemy units with your Commander your own troops will run you off the road. If you are flying around with the airplane commander, it is really really difficult to hit targets on the ground because the camera keeps trying to recenter on the current altitude you're at.
This is a really fun game. I would love to recommend this game if only the game had proper audio control, proper commander  controls, and at least 5 more unit variations.

A casual point and click game about you and your sister who had to leave your village because of an earthquake that killed your family. You find a fishing village, which is later attacked by pirates, who kidnapped your sister.  You go around the countryside making your self useful to the various villages and cities while searching for your sister.  The villagers send you out to kill creatures, collect mushrooms, fruit, herbs, crabs, etc.  The game is a lot better than the first Hero of the Kingdom, but there is still a lot of back and forth that may annoy some Gamers.  The graphics are decent. It may be hard to see mushrooms and other items especially if you wear glasses or have bad eye sight or is impatient.  So take your time and look around. Sound effects is really good. You can hear the different effects for villages,  and cities you visit. The music is standard. Overall, this is a really good game to have in your library. 9/10.

I had my worries of the game especially considering how multiple gaming review sites just loved to tear it a new one. I found however a particular repeating element and pattern that struck me the wrong way in most of them. The major complaints often revolve around repetition and easy difficulty structure. The learning curve is rather flat while taking the time to solve mysteries and crimes is often called child's play at that. I hate to use this term but it just feels so rather Meta in the face of the pace the game seems to give off. Salem just looks so ghostly inviting and everywhere has the potential for you to take the time and admire the lives of the still living. At the same time it just doesn't feel like a burden to get to the next part of the story and become all the more curious of the world around you.
Even the collectables have merit in the stories they tell. It just seems that a great number of people expected a rather explosive and mind bending experience. Murdered: Soul Suspect is like a brisk walk through the undead and spiritual park. It's a pleasant walk. It has a great way of not stifling the flow it has set up and the characters you come to find along the way give a curious nuance to the atmosphere. Would I say the game is flawless or addictive? No, I do not believe it is an extreme grabber that you can't let go of. It's more like that book you've been wanting to read for awhile and you just finally got down to reading it. Take your time, appreciate the attention to details, and you'll feel all the more rewarded for the investment. If you're more set on something more fast paced and hectic then perhaps another title may be up your alley.

Fair Disclosure: I was a Kickstarter backer of this game.
Remember how games used to look before everything had to be rendered as players went through? No? That's okay, STASIS reminds you how deep and compelling they were. Dismissing this game for it's prerenders and/or it's static viewpoint is a huge mistake, especially if one is into a beautifully crafted story with generous helpings of lore and background to go around.
STASIS starts out much like any other sci-fi horror game: player wakes up in a scene somewhere between the cryogenic thaw scenes of Demolition Man and the gore-tastic parts of Event Horizon (one of which you should watch if you like sci-fi horror, the other if you're a fan of "did anyone read the script before argreeing to this" horror). From there the game follows some tropes (oh, all these logs mention not going to this place... guess where I'm headed) but manages to keep a steady pace to maintain interest. Some of the puzzles can be a bit of a pain to get through but luckily there are generous hints not only in the logs but 'on' them as well (when you see it for the first time you'll get it). Unfortunately, there are some typical "oh, those things have to be combined, strange" moments (let's face it, it's a staple of point-and-click adventure games) but aside from those and some story tropes the game is definately worth a few playthroughs (once to get to the end, once to find all the ways to die because achievements, and once to try to figure out what the heck happened at that part).

Hero of the Kingdom 2 is a slightly better version of its predecessor. If you like casual adventure games then you will find about 5 to 7 hours of enjoyment here. Bottom line: Pick this game up if your looking for something to mindlessly occupy your time for a lazy afternoon.
Just like Hero of the Kingdom 1, HotK2 (that acronym sound like some BA skis) is a click your own adventure. This time around the there is more crafting, more collectibles, more quests, and infinitely more clicking. I have to be honest, the clicking is ridiculous! Example 1: Some of the game is a lite version of hidden object where you have to find say, eggs. You click the eggs, an animation shows the eggs being taken, then an icon of the eggs appear and you must then click the icon of the eggs to obtain them. Given the fact there are about 1,000 hidden objects in the game that's 2,000 clicks you have to do! That's just one example. Most tasks within HotK2 requires 2 to 4 clicks to complete. This was a problem in the first game, only it feels like it's gotten worse. This is probably due to the extended length of the game.
The writing has improved over HotK1. Now instead of the storyline reading like it was written by a 12 year old boy and edited by a 6 year old girl, it's more like a 16 year old boy wrote it and was edited by a 14 year old girl. Grammar has improved. Spelling errors were down. The general story was more in-depth. However, like I said, it's still juvenile, just less primary school. There will be no awards for storytelling here, but you'll be less apt to skip over all the story as in before.
The game as a whole is fun! The constant clicking, predictable story aside, HotK2 has a way of pulling you in and making you want to complete every facet of it. I grabbed this up for $3. For 7 hours playtime with 100% achievements, I feel like it was a good investment. If you're looking for something that can waste away a rainy day, you've found it.

Mass Effect 2 is pretty goddamn great. ME1 was fun, but the combat was either easy (if you were playing an Adapt) or tedious and bad (if you weren't). 2's combat is way improved, with biotics getting a much needed nerf, which actually makes them more fun to use. Gun combat is leagues ahead of the first. The dialogue is still good, with some quite funny or interesting incidental conversations, and your choices are surprisingly well reflected. However, the main issue (aside from giving you a morally grey choice and then deciding one is good and one is evil) is the plot. Playing a paragon early on feels like going against what the game intends. It gets better later, but between the prevalence of renegade interupts and the inconsistency of some paragon morals, it feels like the game is written for a renegade. It's also a bit too much like filler- things are basically the same at the end of ME2 as ME1. But still, some amazing sequences and great gameplay make this well worth it.

Plot 5/10:
The game relies on one of the most overused tropes in regards to Salem's history for it's primary plot. At least in high schools in Mississippi, The Crucible is required reading. Any experience with it and you'll have guessed the killer's name by the time you first meet. The only thing that will come as a shock is who the person targets and manipulates.
Gameplay: 4/10
It was playable, but the audio would skip occasionally in cutscene, the game stuttered regularly, and the "stealth or not" portions were absurdly easy. You'll be forgetting to hold down a button for getting rid of demons more than you'll actually be bothered by them. Also, the walking through walls, possessing people, and such loses its flair pretty quickly. Especially considering half of the NPCs share the exact same 2 lines of inner monologue when you possess them even though they're 15 feet apart, and that's not exaggeration. Plus, you'll spend the majority of the extremely short story trying to look for the clues that require you to aim directly at them before the prompt appears. Extremely frustrating at times.
Overall, your best bet is to not waste your money till this game goes on sale.

Honestly, this game is HARD to get behind, I was sold from trailers and screenshots, thinking it would be a mix between Supreme Commander (Which it is, but not the ways you expect.) and Hawken (Yes i'm comparing it to that as well.)
And honestly, it may be good in some places, but those good, are faaaaar outweighed by the bad.
Firstly, this game hasn't been properly optimized in my opinion, i can run ARMA 3, ARK, hell.. even Elite Dangerous with barely or no issues frames, or stability wise.
With this, i struggle to even get 15 frames on the lowest settings possible, along with constant crashes. It may be because my computer is Bipolar in a way. But i think this is optimization issues honestly.
Secondly, the UI and Controls are HORRIBLE. Oh my god i have never found a game that didn't know if it wanted to have stiff, or loose controls. Some moments i'm perfectly fine and i turn ever so gently to find myself doing a full 360 turn.

Plus, you need the premium currency (i.e. someone had to pay real money for it) to buy slots for weapons or frames if you want more than a handful of items.
Or . . .  you can just drop some real money to get the item prebuilt, with double the moding capacity, and slot to go along with it.

Words cant describe why you should buy this so,here is a pancake recipe
100g plain flour
2 egg
300ml semi-skimmed milk
1 tbsp sunflower oil
or vegetable, plus extra for frying
pinch salt
Blending in the flour: Put the flour and a pinch of salt into a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the middle, then pour in about 50ml milk and 1 tbsp oil. Start whisking from the centre, gradually drawing the flour into the eggs, milk and oil. Once all the flour is incorporated, beat until you have a smooth, thick paste. Add a little more milk if it is too stiff to beat.
Finishing the batter: Add a good splash of milk and whisk to loosen the thick batter. While still whisking, pour in a steady stream of the remaining milk. Continue pouring and whisking until you have a batter that is the consistency of slightly thick single cream. Traditionally, people would say to now leave the batter for 30 mins, to allow the starch in the flour to swell, but there’s no need.
Getting the right thickness: Heat the pan over a moderate heat, then wipe it with oiled kitchen paper. Ladle some batter into the pan, tilting the pan to move the mixture around for a thin and even layer. Quickly pour any excess batter into a jug, return the pan to the heat, then leave to cook, undisturbed, for about 30 secs. Pour the excess batter from the jug back into the mixing bowl. If the pan is the right temperature, the pancake should turn golden underneath after about 30 secs and will be ready to turn.
Flipping pancakes: Hold the pan handle, ease a fish slice under the pancake, then quickly lift and flip it over. Make sure the pancake is lying flat against base of the pan with no folds, then cook for another 30 secs before turning out onto a warm plate. Continue with the rest of the batter, serving them as you cook or stack onto a plate. You can freeze the pancakes for 1 month, wrapped in cling film or make them up to a day ahead.

FyI, I originally bought the game on Desura about one and a half years ago, so I haven't yet played it on Steam.
The game is reminicent of old Fallout titles and similar games, top-down, turnbased combat, intesresting background story that leaves just as many questions as it answers. I'm not even perfectly sure it's postapocalyptic, though that is a rather obvious conclusion.
The setting takes place underground, in a multi-layered subway system and assorted underground caves. After the first Quests, the player can choose his path almost freely,  visiting a variety of lovingly crafted locations and making himself useful for a variety of factions and 'interesting' personalities in the face of first an earthquake and then an invasion. What you choose to do is decided by both morality and money, and includes fetch quests, investigations, espionage, and hit missions.
Or become a champion in the arena.
Combat is turnbased, with an action point system not unlike the one in old fallout games, Wasteland, etc;
You can choose between a variety of melee weapons, throwables, firearms, energy weapons, and Psionics.
A relatively extensive crafting system can be exploited for superior equipment, including items you can't even get any other way, but you might pay for it with a skill deficiency somewhere else.
The game invokes pleasant memories of older games without being outdated or clunky, and the visuals, while simple, do well to convey the atmosphere of the world. A special mention for the music, which is certainly top notch and fits the respective scenery very well.
In total, I definitely recommend this game; there's just not many like it, and it sports good atmosphere and solid mechanics. A warning to Loot-OCD-Practioneers, however: The carry-weight limit and tendency of traders to only buy what they can actually sell might leave you rather encumbered.
Tl;dr:
Classic Top Down RPG with great atmosphere. A good buy for fans of the genre, and definitely worth a look for others.

Release update: The game is out and it is as good as ever!
With AAA publishers continuing to spew out mediocrity in the name of "next gen" progress, this title is a breath of fresh air and is shaping up to be one of the best games of this generation.
Those who have played the early fallouts (specifically Fallout and Fallout 2) will be immediately familiar with this game.
Here is a list of my observations/opinions on this game (in no particular order):
1. Great setting, atmosphere and world building. The settlements, NPCs, etc make sense within the gameworld.
2. All the game systems are well designed - The character system, crafting, turn based combat, stealth, C&C, story, exploration and  XP systems are all well thought out.
3. While the graphics are not pretty (they are adequate), the sound is excellent and really adds to the setting.
4. The game is quite difficult (good), especially early on, and the difficulty curve varies depending on the character build (as each build has different strengths and weaknesses). As long as the player thinks through all available options for each encounter and uses their character's available tactical options, the difficulty is generally manageable. This aspect may turn off some players.
5. Unlike fallout, the combat is more tactical and not easily exploitable, which helps maintain the challenge throughout the game.
6. There are some areas where the game isn't as great: No pacifist approach & linear starting area sequence are a couple of examples.
7.  Overall, the game is very stable and there is a lot of content.
8.  Amazing value for the asking price.
Highly recommended for those who want a deep and great CRPG experience.

Warshift is one of those gems that is hidden deep within Steam. it's a RTS/3rd person shooter hybrid made by one man by all accounts. Once your in game that one fact should amaze you. This game feels feature rich for the £5 I paid for it. It also looks amazing, the videos and screen shots above dont lie. If anything the game tries to mix to many elements together to create its world.
The campaign sees the player take control of a variety of hero units which they can seamlessly jump in and out of at any point during a mission. Switching instantly from RTS to 3rd person mode if you need to boss the battlefield. This unit levels up every map and has a large variety of upgrades and almost RPG type paths to take. You also must take control of The ARK. The Ark is your mobile home base that when grounded can create factories and defensive turrets etc to place near control points. When capped these supply resources much in the same why they do in Dawn of War 2 Multiplayer. From these factories you can then produce a wide variety of units to attack the enemy or hold your control points.
It's all executed at a frenetic pace and feels like what Command and Conquer 4 should have been.
If I have any complaints and so far there few. It would be the enemy AI. Even on easy, for a RTS veteran it can quickly overwhelm you in a straight up fight. A  little adjust ment there would be nice.
Also would be nice to see a little intro movie explaining the story but this is only dressing.
SKirmish mode has 6 maps versus AI and I even found a few Multiplayer maps.
I would say it COULD be the best money you spend in the Steam sale.

Stasis is an isometric point and click adventure game. It's a sci fi horror, so think Dead Space Event Horizon ran by Weyland-Yutani wrapped up and served as Sanitarium. Quite nice if you go for that creepy disgusting wtf-is-this feeling.
You, John Marachek, go to stasis induced sleep next to your family only to wake up, quite brutally, on a completely alien ship next to some unknown, and also dead, people. You travel through the empty innards of that ship to find your family and uncover the horrifying secrets of Weyland-Yutani, erm, I mean Cayne Corporation.
VISUALS
First thing first, forget about your fancy gfx settings. Actually forget about any gfx settings as there are none. Well, you can change brightness, but other than that you cannot even change the resolution. Fortunately, the lack of settings doesn't mean that the game looks bad. Apart from the often stiff animations everything looks positively creepy with spaceship interiors splattered with blood here and mysterious research facility of unspeakable horrors there.
AUDIO
Music and sound effects are fitting for most part, but there are a few places where music becomes might annoying. Fortunately these are few and far between. More often than not the audio is adding that additional layer of creepiness with occassional cackling pipes, distant scream or mutant roar.
GAMEPLAY
Is basically what you could expect from a point and click adventure game. Most of the time you are either pointing or clicking. The story is not the greatest ever told, but it is solid and has a few twists. It is mostly told by the discarded PDA and log entries, so some reading is involved. The puzzles are rather logical and can be solved by, less or more creative, thinking rather by using everyt item on everything. It took me 8hrs to finish, with reading all the PDA entries and paying some attention to environment and without being very much stuck anywhere.
Recommended for fans of The Fall, Event Horizon, and anyone who thinks point and click Dead Space could be fun.

For lovers of Horror/Sci-fi who don't mind an isometric point and click adventure, this is definitely a must.
There are some problems with the game, such as music glitches and resolution, but for a game done by basically 2 people, this is an awesome indie that is worth every penny even without sales.
The game has a really dark and creepy atmosphere, which goes great. The art is fantastic, so is the voice acting. Often you feel the protagonist pain and misery just by the great voice acting. I felt very connected to the protagonist and creeped out by the tense moments you go through, having to do some pretty scary and gruesome stuff.
Also, the game was developed through 5 years and it seems the developers paid a lot of attention to how the story is given to us, so it is very detailed and careful on the information it gives us. Generally it's well written with a few flawed cliche/stereotypical characters, such as the magalomaniacal scientist playing God, but we can get past that and enjoy the overall experience.
Also, we might expect a sequel, which is very exciting. So if Stasis is a success we might have an even better second game? Let's hope so.
Buy the game and enjoy the experience.

This is a nice laid back old-style click'n'point adventure game. Although the available actions and game mechanics are somewhat limited compared to other (older) games in the same genre, it delivers a surprisingly rich gaming experience after all. The storytelling is superb, and the incredibly tense atmosphere and depressed tone of the setting keeps you on your toes all the time. Always something to explore, always something to look out for, and always something that can kill you. After a while it sort of becomes a game in itself, trying to discover new horrible ways to die.
The graphical sets and the sound designs are brilliant, and could easily match any science fiction blockbuster tbh. It's been very long since I've played a game that has such haunting audio visuals as this little game.
Who would have imagined that a "simple" click'n'point could make a grown man nervously jumpy like a little girl :(
This is certainly a game all science fiction fans should have in their collection.

Stasis is a well-realized point-and-click adventure that stays very true to its narrative roots. And this narrative - which is uncompromising sci-fi horror - was honestly a treat to experience. It actually manages to pull a deft slight-of-hand by presenting you with two stories in one. The first story is the one that is presented to you through overt gameplay interactions and as a history and series of subsequent events understood (and, frequently, commented on) by your in-game avatar. But this is classic unreliable narration. The reality of the situation, which mirrors the standard narrative in large chunks but diverges on important details, is revealed only to the player via journal excerpts that the in-game avatar seems to overlook.
My main point of criticism is that the isometric perspective is pulled back too far. As a result, interactive objects are smaller than they need to be and are easily overlooked. When you enter a new room it often isn't clear where your character model is standing. Furthermore you are freqeuntly in areas that feature large blocks of dark, unused space all around the rim of the screen. Why does the player need to see all of this unused space? This isn't a tactical RTS. In fact a more intimate presentation - i.e. closer figures and finer details - would have served the game experience well by not only alleviating the above minor frustrations but also by being a better psychological representation of the claustrophobic circumstances (you are trapped aboard an unknown space ship).
The game does a great job of sustaining atmosphere throughout, and I think a lot of this has to do with the strength of the story and the writing (esp. dialogue). I'm a writer so I'm used to wincing my way through inane and implausible dialogue. Little wincing was required here except when a rather cookie-cutter villian started issuing canards (you can hear some of these in the video trailer). A few odd intonations aside, the voice acting is fairly solid throughout. It's a point-and-click adventure so, yes, there are a few finicky puzzles. However I resorted to a walkthrough on only two occasions - BOTH times I was stuck because I had missed picking up an object from a previous area (there's that resolution/distance problem).
A 7-8 hour treat for sci fi aficionados who like their fiction hard-edged and very dark.

Dinosaur hunt; Africa Contract is a First person game in which you Kill Dinosaurs. That being said i havn't played or updated the game for a while and will probably wait for quite some time before making another review. to give the developers more time to update and fix the game. But i feel as though this game needs to be reviewd at this current point in time aswell.This review wont be to attack the developers or the game, it is strictly a review on how the game is at it's current point.
Gameplay- 3/10
To me it's really repetitive and simple, which may not be a bad thing alot of people enjoy the simple games. However, personally i enjoy something a bit more intracate. but that's just a personal opionion. The dinosaurs all feel the same, apart from looks and sizes they act the same and have the same movement paterns. The game does not feel immersive and the in game sounds just don't fit in.  But again the developers ( Racing Bros) are doing a great job at constantly updating the game and making it a little bit better each update.
Graphics- 4/10 The graphics don't look to bad. the textures might not be the best but at least ( from my knowlage) Racing Bros are not taking assets and just plugging them into a game like alot of developers are lately. the sound design doesn't feel as though it fits in with the game as ( from when i last played) the dinosaurs all sounded the same. the map design isn't to bad but it could use some work as the areas feel lifeless and plain.
Story- 2/10
From what i gathered there is no real story in this game, you just kill dinosaurs and sometimes zombies/mobs. The campaign mode within the game is just finding a dinosaur within the map and killing it and repeating until you get enough kills to enter the next map.
Overall- 6/10
This game does have a decent overall score mainly due to the fact that this game is litterally the price of a lollipop. Racing Bros are not asking for much as anyone can easily rack up $1 that being said the game still needs many improvements to sound graphics and gameplay, and if you want something that is simple and cheap then feel free to pay this small amount. However I am still going to give this a negative review mainly because i feel as though the game needs to be completed more before being bought.

I have to say, now that I am approaching by 250th hour, I love this game. Its an amazingly fun game with much to explore and do. Here's a list of Pros and Cons to Ark
Pros
- Hundreds of hours of content
- Many dinos to tame and fight
- Good amounts of lategame progression
- Has the mechanics of a really good survival game
- PVP is okay, but not the most optimized
- Good Modding Community to change up everything if you want more to explore
- You can host a Non-Dedicated session to play with a small few friends and just explore the game in a PVE setting
Cons
- Poorly Optimized, you will need a pretty good pc to run this game efficiently
- Server Browser is a bit problematic
- $60 Price Tag, yeah thats a really big turn-off for many. Buy it when its on sale for 50% off or greater to make it worth
- Paid DLC ontop of a $60 Game, this isn't a triple A title by some big company, adding $20 DLC every few months is highly annoying
- Releasing DLC BEFORE the game was fully released, the expansion Scorched Earth released before the game went out of early access
- Building System is absolutely BROKEN, building your base is at times impossible, with problems and bugs everywhere
So do I recommend it? Hell Yeah!
While it may be buggy and the price tag may be very high, I still love this game. I have been playing since Alpha and have followed it through its whole development. When I say its gotten much better overtime, take my word for it. As for the price, wait for it to be on sale for 50% off or higher, then it is worth. Its a $30 game whos developer decided to try and make a cash cow and spike the price up to $60. Buy the DLC if you want, I did and love them both, but it is NOT necessary to fully enjoy this game. It is tough, frustrating, and downright annoying at times but that is what comes with a survival game like this. I would recommend it to anyone who is down for a challenge, loves dinosaurs, survival games, and PvP. Good Luck out there!

The first game in the Fable franchise, and my favorite. The gameplay can be compared to Elderscrolls, but with a more ballanced approach to gameplay. Stat's are raized by experience (divided up depending on how you kill your enemies), but farther along in the game there isn't really anything keeping you from specializing in all three areas (Strength, Skill (dexterity), and Magic). The idea of Good and Evil play's an important part in the story, allowing you to be either admired or feared. The Lost Chapters is an extention to your story, bringing you to a new land with new adventures. The comedy in the game is carried out through hilarious dialogue, while still maintaining a serrious main storyline. For those who long for a great Action RPG from the past, this is the one for you!

It's a fun game, with a decent story and lots of variety on abilities.
That being said it's still in Alpha (at the time of this review) and lots needs to change.
The game is extremely unbalanced, so if you like sitting around and watching the enemy attack you without you getting any turns for 4 to 10 rounds, then you'll enjoy this game.
The enemies have the same powers and abilities as your team, and will use them to freeze, stun, poison and generally prevent you from attacking or making any actions against them or even at all during combat, with no way to free yourself from the effects, and this is on Explorer Mode.
I'm looking forward to the full release and especially the game master portion of the game, but as of right now it's unbalanced and far too difficult to even get off the starting island, let alone enjoy the rest of the game.
All that being said. I'm having fun playing it when the above noted isn't happening to me at almost every fight. Looking forward to enjoying it much more in the future.

Great action RPG. I liked pretty much everyrhing: story, graphics, gameplay, background music and voiceover. You can "be what you want", buuuut...
SPOILERS?
your alignment does not change the story, apart from some details. Different playthroughs with different alignments are fun just to see the people's reaction and the changes your body go through, but it does not add anything at all to the story.
You can customize your character with hairstyles, mustaches, beards and tattoos.
It does not take a lot of grinding to max out the char stats, and the peculiar thing of the leveling system of Fable is that you grow old as you level up your skills: this makes things a bit awkward, especially when you're older than your big sister, or even your mother.
The trading system is exploitable, so making big money is a piece of cake.
And last, the equipment/item system: it's really nothing special, and a bit of a let down. Weapons have an attack stat and swing/reload speed, armors a defense stat. You can upgrade your weapons, but since you may get really powerful gear here and there you'll not do it often.

This game is absolutely amazing.  Nowadays, games focus too much on action sequences...press "A" repeatedly to break the dog's neck!  However, UnderRail doesn't worry about overrated things like graphics, action sequences, DLC, and other forms of gaming garbage that have become rampant in the industry.
UnderRail is about as old school as it comes (like everyone has already said, think isometric Fallout 2) in CRPGs today.  The combat system is solid, and it fits well with the "Feat" system.  If you are familiar with Fallout's "Perk" system or Elder Scrolls' similiar system, then you'll see that UnderRail has basically that same exact thing built into character creation.
Now, one of the most unique things about UnderRail is that, instead of doing quests and killing things to get experience and level up, you can opt to play the game without that traditional "grinding" to level system in place.  If you choose to play the way the developers intend, then choose the "Oddities" option.  Basically, this means that in order to gain levels and develop your character's stats and feats, you will need to find oddity items throughout the game.  These might drop from monsters after a kill or be hidden in a crate in a dark and dangerous room.  Playing with this leveling system enabled will make you explore places that you might not normally take the time to delve into, and it keeps you constantly looking for that one extra item so that you can get another level.  Personally, this is the only way I play after they added it into the game.  Keep in mind that if you prefer the classic "kill monster, get experience points, repeat and level up" system, then you can totally do that.  Nobody will judge you for your poor, poor choices...we promise...maybe...
I rarely take the time to write reviews...but if story, gameplay, and a genuinely well thought out leveling and character progression system appeals to you...if you miss the difficulty of computer games from days past, then this is one of those diamonds in the rough that I would highly suggest picking up.
I think it is one of my top 3 favorite games.

As a massive fan of point & click adventure games, my favourites being Monkey Island, King’s Quest and Sanitarium I can without a doubt say that STASIS is now among that list. STASIS achieves pretty much everything I love about gaming – fantastic art direction, great visuals, great design, heavy atmosphere and (not always necessary) a very intriguing plot and well written/voiced dialogue. This game has restored a lot of my faith in this industry, great to know minds like this still exist in this industry.
In STASIS you play the role of John Maracheck, a school teacher whom with his family enter hibernation capsules for deep space travel, after which, John wakes up 3 months later alone on a massive, dark and seemingly abandoned ship but soon finds out that he’s not alone. As John, you will need to progress through the ship, which is achieved by exploring and solving puzzles, in pursuit of your family, not knowing of their current state, and with them try find a way off this ship.
STASIS is truly a breath of fresh air, if you are a fan of Sanitarium then getting this would be an absolute no brainer, I’m still lost for words that something like this exists in this era, even more so knowing that it was pulled off by a team of two South African brothers, there really is no excuse for gaming to be in the lackluster and uninspired state it currently resides. Easily the best point & click adventure game since the 90’s in my opinion, a true modern classic.

I just discovered this game and got super excited to find a brand-new dinosaur-themed game for $1. The still shots looked good, and the most recent reviews were positive, so I gave it a shot. I played this game for a few minutes and gave up. The main thing that is bothering me is the primitiveness of the game. The graphics and user interface feel like this game was made 10+ years ago, and not in a good way. The game loaded very slow and the graphics were pretty spotty even for the low level of detail on screen. The dinosaurs are fairly broken. The skin is very rubbery in texture, and their movement animation is bad (walking in place without moving forward, clipping into the player's character when the dinosaur is attacking you). In campaign mode the player can spawn within a few feet of 2-4 giant carnivores. The good news when that happens is that you practically have to run into the dinosaur to get them to notice you. They have more important things to do, like a T-rex that performs the eating animations to an empty patch of grass. There is very little tutorial teaching what the different things mean or how to pick up ammunition/med packs. I gave up after about 20 minutes of playing.
Now, this game WAS only $1, but there are some really great games that are only a dollar (please see below) that you should check out instead.There are a lot of really great dinosaur themed games out there. If you are looking for some suggestions, check out:
ARK:Survival evolved (~$25) a really beautiful survival & dinosaur capturing/riding game with a huge fanbase and a great development team
Carnivores: Dinosaur Hunter Reborn ($15), a very solid dinosaur hunting game based on a very popular series that I played as a kid.
and Orion: Prelude ($1) the best $1 dollar you can spend on steam for hours and hours of cooperative multiplayer dinosaur shoot-em-up action
Buy those instead

John Maracheck's last memory is the fun chat he had with his wife and daughter before going to sleep in a stasis pod for a space trip together: now he wakes up gasping from hypersleep but the room is unfamiliar and dark, the ship vastly different from the one they traveled in...what happened? Where has his family gone? And why are there bodies and signs of violence all around the seemingly abandoend ship?
A great point-and-click adventure making good use of isometric perspective STASIS is a dark, gritty and gore-filled journey through a ghost ship where things are actually way, way worse than they may seem at first.
-lovely art style, the ship feels really gritty and abandoned with trash, broken parts, slaughtered bodies, flickering lights and malfunctioning computers
-top notch sound department, every area has its own sounds from creaking iron to cacophonic audio from monitors, rumbling from the ship, echoing screams or noises that'd be coming from worse sources: soundtrack is also truly fitting
-great writing, there's lots of meticulously written PDAs for you to go over that detail the story of the ship and what's happening in it while also containing puzzle clues: most items you can interact with or look at are also described with a very nice style
-art style, sound and writing contribute to creating a great atmosphere: the Groomlake truly feels alive and its dark interiors convey a sense of dread and menace seldom seen anywhere else
-the whole plot, slowly fed to you through events and things you'll read, is truly done well and keeps you engaged and on edge from start to finish: the ending sequence is also very powerful
-overall the puzzles are quite nice and, for the most part, remain challenging without being too taxing
-the game doesn't refrain from throwing liberal violence (both on the body and mind) over the protagonist and does in a very graphic way at times: the things you'll read about or experience yourself can hit home with quite a punch
-no resolution options, the game looks a tad fuzzy and loses some details due to this
-a couple of puzzles were honestly a bit too hard for my liking, sometimes this was made worse by the aforementioned resolution where a small item could not be easily noticed: this either leads to trying all objects on everything in the scene, a dull pixel hunting or a quick trip on the forums to ask for help...thankfully this happened only 2-3 times
-a few suicides look a bit silly and unrealistic
-some animations look a bit unconvincing
-could really use a skip dialogue function for when you have to replay scenes containing them
I had a tremendous time with STASIS, the game has a truly great story but sadly pointing out its good points would require spoilers: let's just say it manages to give you a good sense of urgency through the whole adventure and that it's as dark and terrifying as the rooms it is set in. The level of fear, violence and body-horror the game throws your way also makes for a memorable horror experience in its purest form, one where graphic slaughter is freely paired with psychological horror.
It's a bit of a shame that the fixed resolution doesn't fully do justice to the great art while getting in the way of puzzles at times: said puzzles can also leave you truly stuck when you meet a couple that feel obtuse or overly vague. When this happens the gameplay can suffer a bit as the story grinds to an halt while you desperately scramble for a solution.
These few issues can be easily overlooked when you consider the many things STASIS has to offer: it's a good game by itself but also a truly great horror experience that I fully recommend. Buy it, play it, it'll stay with you even after you've finished it.

This game is overall very fun. However, the gameplay can get repetitive. This isn't automatically bad the way it is done, but if you dislike the gameplay to begin with then it just gets worse the more you play.
The fun part about the game is the sheer amount of unlockables and secrets. You can play through just New Game and New Game + modes and discover new things even after your 7th time of playing through it. The buying/selling system is very simple for how complicated it is to open a real store, but I suppose in an age/world without taxes and math is basically just simple addition and subtraction it does make sense. The story does not seem strange at all in how it is translated which is rare for Japanese games.
The dungeon crawling part of the game is also fun and almost doubles as a game within a game. Not only is it fun but you can select from more than 5 characters to level up, raise affection within your store of, and play as within the dungeons. Not only that but play within more than 4 dungeons. Including 2 challenge dungeons.
Then as if that was not enough there are a ton of extra modes in the game making the time you can play the game virtually limitless. However, you have to unlock them by beating the story.
My only gripe is that the store and dungeon both lack true depth. For an indie game this is still better than the vast majority but it was so close to just being a perfect game.

Pros:
-Compelling story, made me sit down and play though it in one sitting, amazing.
-Gameplay, if you like to walk around and discover everything then this is the game for you. It never gets dull, slow or too fast. Demons are there to change up gameplay and overall I enjoyed being a exorcist.
-Graphics, beautiful game, love the art, everything looks great.
-I found a few Just Cause 2 posters in the game.
-Even though it's supernatural it doesn't feel fake/childish.
-Writing, for the most part, was done very well.
-Made me want to help the lost souls and feel rewarded for doing so.
-Examples about people who throw their life away.
-Good ending.
Cons:
-Short, only about 5 hours if you stick to the story and probably close to 6-7 if you want to 100% the game.
-Character development, sometimes it felt like characters weren't developed enough for me but I like to know full blown backgrounds, I wouldn't say it was bad though.
-Occasional frame drops.
Overall: Solid game, would definitely recommend. Good luck in the afterlife!!

Avaliable only on computer, unlike it's follow-ups, this PC game is still as good. My only faults are: that it was made in the dark ages of gaming when nearly all games had male protagonists, so there isn't any female option to play as; and that the people are fairly boring (none of the NPCs have as much character background as those in Fable 2 and 3, and you've no dog as a companion). The NPCs also follow you around with simple interactions and have hearts over their heads to indicate romanceable or not. It's not Fable 3 bad, but it's certainly not as good as Fable 2. Finally, clothing is fairly limited in this game unlike its successors, as the outfits of Knight, bandit, etc, do not have dye options. Plus, it also seems like a carry-on in the series; you're required to attain a bandit outfit from boxes in order to gain entry into the bandits' camp, which is very similar to Fable 3. However, to be fair, in Fable 3 you have the options of dying the outfit and changing your hairstyle more. Plus, you never actually meet any Knights in this game, or in the others for that matter, so that outfit is made practically meaningless. Basically, Fable 1 therefore mostly just has showy outfits for the player.
However, if you're a fan and want to find out how it began (I played 3, 2, and then 1), then this would be a good choice. The story-line is interesting, if a tad cliche, with the main character's family being separated by a bandit attack; you still have moral choices (good or bad actions, skinny or tubby, etc); there is certainly more information in Fable 1, as on the menu you can find how many houses you own to whether you're defined as hetro/homosexual through your interactions (information that isn't present in Fable 2 and 3!); you're more likely to gain scars and die during the battles in this one, as the gameplay is more difficult; and the graphics are quite good for a game this old.
Further, with the release of Fable 1 Anniversary on xbox360, the graphics are even further improved if you're more inclined to spend a little more and play on the console. The pixels are more noticeably defined on the console, but there are known glitches and the developers didn't add anything to the series. You would literally be spending your money on just lighter graphics. This PC version is just as good. In fact, it's better because it has more of a history.
So, all in all, the PC Fable 1: Lost chapters is a good game if you're looking for an intro into playing the later series or you're in want of playing a humorous game (the quests certainly do fit that bill).

This a fairly classic noir story -- with a supernatural twist. I've seen the reviews that put the game at around a 5-6 (mediocre) and on one hand I can see that. As it currently stands, I would say wait to purchase this title.
The game shows great promise, and its clear that there is much love and care going into it from the developer, however the game is not well balanced and most people I believe will find it a frustrating experience, especially in the beginning. I really wanted to believe all these glowing reviews but I think many people are looking at this game through rose tinted glasses.
Whats good: The combat sound effects are nice and impactful. The combat itself is decent, not amazing but good. There are a large number of skills that can be learned. There is a unique level up system that can be interesting (not sure I love it but I am sure many will). There is an almost overwhelming number of items to be found and used in the game (for crafting, tools, weapons, etc.).
Whats not great: You are an army of one, there are no followers or companions in this game (that I have found anyway). There are many weapons...but you wont be able to use most of them AT ALL initially because there is an arbitrary skill level requirement in place... a skill level requirement even for basic assault rifles that you wont hit probably until level 5-6. The combat is HARD for a newbie. You will quickly run out of low level creatures to level up on in the starting area and if you wont develop your character perfectly you will need to start over as you will get stuck, unable to defeat the more powerful enemies in surrounding areas.
While the combat is fun it is missing some things that would make it great, such as a cover mechanic, or positions like prone or crouched. Most enemies will make short work of you, even with good armor and a decent weapon you will get overwhelmed by numbers quite often. It is very easy to wander beyond the confines of what your character can handle without the most thoughtful and dedicated build. I appreciate challenging combat but it would be nice if there was a mix of challenges, rather than everything being in♥♥♥♥♥♥mode.
The economy is poor, shop keepers will charge outrageous prices for staples like bullets and bandages. We are talking like trading your pristine handgun, a set a armor, and a substantial amount of money for like 10 bandages or a handful of bullets. Additionally, shopkeepers wont take just any old thing in trade, only certain items that they want or need. That means you need to find a specific shop keeper to get rid of junk, or you wont be selling it at all. Mercantile skill does not seem to help either, perhaps not working yet?
The story so far is underwhelming me. In fact there doesnt seem to be much of a story at all, just missions that you do for your home base. However I am going to reserve judgement here as I have only gotten to the Junkyard which I assume is pretty early in the game. Similarly though, the dialogue seems pretty limited and I dont seem to be building any interesting relationships with...well ANY of the characters in the game. This also might be something that opens up later on, so I am reserving judgement there too for the moment.
The graphics are intentionally retro. I am neutral on this wave of "authentic" old school graphics in games, it doesnt bother me but  I also dont kneel down and praise the limited pixel gods when I see them. I personally would prefer more colorful graphics and more/better character animations but I dont think the gameplay is hampered by them. All in all graphics seem to hold up conistently through the different characters and locations in the game which is nice.
I was not a fan of the music so I turned that down low after not too long. It wasnt bad, just a bit repetitive and not really my style.
This has the potential to be a really excellent game, its just not there quite yet.

Pros:the game and each state/region has its own unique feel. lots of familiarities with ETS2 fans will like, but also a lot of differences I was not expecting. Great scenery. bottom line ETS2 fans have probably already bought this, and if you have not you need to.
Focusing more on the cons to expect:the ai is very dumb. I imagine it will improve but they love to run red lights, they still cant merge and overall it feels if anything a tad worse than ETS2. not game breaking, but should and probably will be improved.
the roads arent toally accurate, which is to be expected, but the instantaneous merging onto the interstate-more so in CA than NV-is not good or realistic in urban areas and bugs me personally. combined with the dumb ai I find more often than not the best way to enter traffic is to just gun it,  hang on, and hope you dont have a crash.
Building on that the one major red flag I have with this game is that there should never, ever be intersections on an interstate but we find several here. modders will probably address it and it doesnt hurt the game significantly, but it iritates me on a personal level because it could easily been avoided, there just no reason to have built the map that way.
only other con I have is they used the sam AI drivers, seeing the same avatars seems lazy and all the crazy eastern european names seem out of place. Again, not game breaking, just a gripe. and they can probably change them just like they did in ETS or I am fine just dealing with it.
Another bigger issue, the 2 trucks is not hurting my feelings personally because I know they are working on it, and we will get mods very shortly. a couple truck mods are already ported over here on release day. but the customization is just not enough right now. you will have some new options not seen in ETS, so that's good, but it really needs more lights and tuning.
Finally, even though we started seeing turn arrows at intersections in ETS2, there are not any here. it can be a problem, and back to the AI they really love to run these 3 at a time. combined with bigger collision fines you really need to watch these guys.

For those that weren't aware of Metro: Last Light its first time around, the game is a direct sequel to Metro 2033, with the plot being set forth by the last moments of 2033. Russia has been decimated by nuclear war, and the only way people were able to survive was to turn the underground metro system into makeshift settlements. Above ground, animals have mutated into horrific beasts, and mysterious psychic beings called the Dark Ones lurk both above ground and below. In Metro 2033: Last Light the monsters aren’t the only danger, as different factions from Neo-Nazis to Commies and beyond are all duking it out for a doomsday device in a civil war for control of Russia’s remains. It’s up to Artyom, the player character, to learn more about the still-mysterious Dark Ones and try to keep relative peace throughout the metro. I really enjoyed the narrative. While the plot itself isn’t terribly original, the world and characters are expanded in the way a good movie sequel grows things not simply for growth’s sake, but to make the player feel even more like they’re in a living, breathing place.
What makes Last Light shine isn’t how many things go boom or how many monsters get pumped full of lead. I mean there’s definitely action, and when it’s there it is satisfying, but where the game series as a whole really succeeded was in creating a palpable atmosphere dense with despair, anxiety, and powerlessness. In some ways Last Light improved on the immersion of Metro 2033 through fully first person cut scenes, expanding the game’s universe, and greatly improved graphics that brought out each spiderweb and puddle of mud.
With the narratives and worlds so tied together it seemed a bit jarring that gameplay took such a sudden change in direction. Thankfully herein lies, in my opinion, the biggest positive about Last Light’s re-release treatment. Now fans of both styles can be happy, as the game lets people choose from the get-go whether they’d like to play the more action-oriented style of the original, or boost up enemy damage and scale back the amount of resources available to play in the style of 2033.
Unfortunately some of the other improvements that Redux boasts end up being largely inconsequential. While graphics technology has improved noticeably since the franchise’s freshman effort in 2010, I really didn’t notice anything looking particularly better in this version than in the Last Light of 2013. I’m sure that if compared side by side there’s probably a few nicer textures and models here and there, but all in all tech just hasn’t developed enough since then to make the visuals a viable reason to upgrade. Don’t, however, confuse that for me being displeased with the way things look. Though the game takes place in underground tunnels and barren wastelands, the game still manages to keep the screen from turning into the brown soup that so many desolate games do.
The art direction helps things too. Everything from the weapons to the underground "buildings" feel ready to fall apart at any moment, and the various people drinking around fires, shopping, and just generally going about their daily lives give the settlements in particular an organic, personable vibe that pull you into the world of Metro that much more. So while none of this is particularly different from the original release to Redux, it’s still pretty darned good.
Whether or not you find Metro: Last Light Redux worth the money is going to depend entirely on what you’re buying it for. If you’re someone who’s never played the game, or if you’re someone like me that liked 2033 but didn’t appreciate the pacing changes the sequel brought, then yes, pull the trigger. The game becomes much more of a survival-horror title with the new available options, and if you’re new you can try both styles and decide for yourself. Otherwise, there’s really no reason to prefer the original over this remastering. The audio visual improvements are modest, and the added content of the DLCs are relatively miniscule. All in all, I myself had a great time with the title, and the Metro franchise is still one nuclear winter I never want to turn to spring.

I am rating the game STASIS here, and my rating is "don't like". I will give you the reasons why.
Pros:
+In my opinion, the game creates a dark and well planned atmosphere, most of the graphics fit in, also the futuristic environment... well done by the devs.
+There are no bugs, and everything is done with voice comments by the participating characters.
Cons:
-The game is short. REALLY short. I finished it in less than 6 hours. When i thought about playing it again, i figured out it is a linear story, so... the story is ok, but not THAT good to play it all over again.
-25€ for less than 6 hours? It's a personal decision, but in my opinion, it's not worth the money.
-In this game, you will find a lot of PDAs which tell you some parts of the story, and what happened to some characters in this game. The story is well told, BUT: if i sum up all the time i spent for reading the story in the PDAs (which don't give you any useful information for your progress in the game at all), i guess i can reduce my pure playing time to less than 5 hours.
-Achievements are mostly about how you can die or kill yourself in a game where survival seems to be important. Since the story is linear, i am not going to play it again and try to kill me in every possible way. Doesn't seem fun to me.
-Dialogues can't be skipped, and the game doesn't allow any player input during some of them. Can be annoying if you died just after a dialogue and then have to listen to a crying guy all over again.
-Coming to death: The story is about
The only way to die is because of your own stupidity (like HEY, there is a closed door with toxic gas behind it... let me open the door! You know what i mean).
-No graphic settings despite gamma and contrast.
-Some of the things you need (this contra is a point of discussion, i know that) are a bit difficult to see, since there is no button to highlight interesting spots. There are some glowing points at some spots, but not all of them. That sometimes results in a search all over the screen to check if you didn't miss something.
-Final summary: This game is just not scary. If you read the cons above, you will figure out that there is like no situation that may scare you, and even jumpscares (if you want to call them like that... snore) are pretty predictable.
My recommendation: Invest your money into something else. This game is not that bad at all, but around 25€ is way too much for this game.

I vaguely remember playing through
about a year ago. It was a blast of casual RPG adventure and I played it through in a couple of evenings. The second instalment is best described to the players of the original game by "more of the same": Light-hearted adventuring in a fantasy-lite setting, being a goody-goody adventurer who has great deeds in his near future. I'd roll in a casual take on the hidden object genre as well.
Storyline is also fairly similar to the original: the protagonist has basically lost everything but he's an honest, hard-working dude so he's not complaining and instead just starts getting stuff done. Then everything goes down the drain again and he has to go save not only his sister but basically the whole civilized world. Being the embodiment of righteousness he's going to help every beggar, farmer and sovereign along the way, even the shady kinds because of "the greater good".
Game mechanics are also familiar. To do stuff the protagonist has a bunch of properties like health, fame and money that he uses to get the dirty business done. Most of the work you can do is clearly shown on the map, and this includes talking to people, trading or doing quests. Usually business takes its toll in the form of reducing health, tools or some of the items the protagonist hoards and hauls around everywhere he goes. You will learn that, controversially, eating different foods and sleeping in quirky places makes you stronger. You've also got abilities (like fishing or foraging) and areas of knowledge (like pearl diving) that allow you to do more stuff on the map if you've got the right tools.
The areas of knowledge allow you to play a kind of hidden object minigame. Take the example of the pearl diving: when you learn it, a bunch of seashells with pearls inside them appear in the water areas. Clicking them gets you pearls. Unlike quests, these are not highlighted but they also don't require any additional tools to collect. Merciful for achievement hunters, there are always couple more than required of each object on the map.
When doing dirty business, all that is required is that you have enough health, money and whatever else is required for the quest. There's otherwise no chance of failure (but your tools sometimes break afterwards). Because of this the story can progress at a fast pace. I think I only had a short pause on progression when I found that I could break the economy by producing ridiculous amounts of flour and later lumber and trade them for surplus gold. The resulting several thousand gold coins made sure that I didn't need to care much about money for the rest of the game.
It took me couple of evenings, i.e. about 6.5 hours to finish the game and find everything for the achievements. I had to keep it rolling for a couple of extra hours for the last cards.
Hero of the Kingdom 2, like its predecessor, is really a game of happy thoughts. Curious how being a fictional goody-goody guy is able to arouse a nice, warm feeling inside of you. Both games would probably work well playing with a child, even more so if they can read. While I got mine on sale I would even recommend this game for the full price: that's how nice it was.

STASIS is a science fiction horror themed isometric point and click adventure game which takes place aboard the Groomlake, a deep space research vessel that belongs to Cayne Corporation. The game has a very gloomy and dark atmosphere to it and it seems to be inspired by various popular sci-fi horror games and movies such as Alien and Dead Space.
In STASIS, you take control of John Maracheck, a school teacher which awakes from cryogenic stasis and finds himself on an unknown ship, the Groomlake. Soon enough, John finds that something has gone terribly wrong aboard the ship and he is surrounded by nothing but death, blood and destruction all around him and he is driven by the fear for his family safety.
The main gameplay element of STASIS, as with any other point and click adventure type of games, is of course, puzzle solving. I can’t remember exactly how many puzzles are in the game but most of them are solvable by finding out certain items and combining them or using them on some background object or something on the environment around you in some way and surprisingly enough, even though I got stuck on some of these sections, afterwards I felt like it all made sense in a way and it wasn’t just some way to stall the player progress. Besides this, you’ll also come across some some other puzzles that involve some actual investigation and sometimes I even had to take notes so I couldn’t forget certain things. That said, STASIS puzzles are not just there for the sake of solving puzzles, they fit in the world and the story and they have a purpose.
For a indie development team, STASIS features a huge amount of high production quality material such as high fidelity cinematics, amazing writing, some of the best rendered backgrounds I’ve seen in recent years and superb sound design. From these aspects I think the ones that contribute most to the game’s amazing atmosphere are the writing and the overall sound design. The dialogue is voice acted but in this case I don’t feel like it’s that much of a strong point, the voice acting isn’t exactly terrible but it isn’t exactly great either in my opinion. The writing however is really neat, and I don’t mean the character’s dialogue, I’m refering to several crew logs you find scattered throughout the levels and to the grotesque and gruesome descriptions of piles of filth that you come across. These provide with you a backstory and fill you in on the history background of the ship, its crew, the company and what happened in previous years creating a believable and credible game world and timeline. I don’t know how they managed it but the sound is quite a big deal in STASIS, no matter where you are you’re constantly hearing things, sometimes you hear screams, sometimes some child’s creepy chanting, probably product of John’s sanity, or even scratches and noises echoing throughout the ship, in some situations, when John witnesses something rather gruesome you can hear his heavy and constant breathing.
Still, I do have a few gripes with the game such as the lack of resolution and V-Sync options on the options menu. One time I had to change my desktop refresh rate so that the game could progress further, it kept freezing at one section. The options menu only has two options, one for brightness and another one for volume and that is it.
Overall STASIS is a great point and click adventure game, it’s very atmospheric, immersive and the puzzles are challenging. It offers around 10 hours worth of gameplay along with an amazing sountrack by Mark Morgan and by the end of it you might be facing some moral dilemmas.

Dustforce is a challenging game to put it lightly. While it is easy to learn it is difficult to master. If you get this game be prepared for how much time you will need to put in to be good at it.
You play a janitor sweeping up and defeating the occasional enemy. The levels themselves are accessed from a nexus, which acts as a level to get to the levels. So, you will need to platform and know how to do certain moves to get to the harder levels. After beating levels, you are graded on your completeness and your Finesse (how smooth your run was), you then receive progress to unlocking keys to get into newer and harder levels. The better you do on the level, the more progress you get to your key.
That is where Dustforce sets itself apart, I think, from most other platformers. The goal of each level isn’t to beat it, its to master it and get the S rank in both Completion and Finesse. So, you can’t just do the level and move on you have to keep doing it and doing it and doing it until you have it perfect. While I did not spend a lot of time with Dustforce, this game is just not for me, I appreciate its difficulty and I had fun when I was able to breeze through levels and not miss a step, but I don’t have the time to put into it to master the game, and I’m just not innately good enough at platformers to do it naturally.
If you like difficult platformers and are the kind of person that loves to perfect their run on any given level, then this game is for you. If you are new to the genre and are looking to use this game as your gateway in, I’m sure there are more good, but less difficult games to get you started.

First of all, as many other reviewers already stated, this is a purely casual point & click game, so move along if you are expecting anything else. But as simple as it is, it's still a very good game if you want to just relax and take your mind off things.
Pros:
+ Very simple gameplay, fitting for all ages. Basically, all you do is click on things. I don't think there is a way to fail in this game.
+ Smooth gameplay. There are no situations where you are stuck in the storyline because you cannot find a tiny little thing on a screen or failed to pick up some item several hours ago.
+ Addictive enough to get you through the story.
+ Original. You don't find many games of this type nowadays.
Cons:
- Mediocre writing. You won't find any interesting dialogs or item descriptions here.
- Very, very cliched story. If you got a hero story cliche in your mind, you are likely to find it here.
- Very short. It took me 7 hours to finish the game and unlock all achievements, but 2-3 hours out of that time I was away from my PC.
Overall, I recommend the game to anyone who just wants to relax in the evening and get a change of pace. Even though it is short, making it any longer would probably bore people out of clicking.

First off, the game is damned impressive to me, considering it's a 1 man job, that part blows me away.
It seems to get some inspiration from "Hostile Waters" and/or "Savage 1 / Savage 2", both of which are games that i really like.
However, i can't recommend the game, it's just functional as a strategy game.
The whole "player controlled commander" idea is great, but the fact that you can't queue structure construction leaves you hopping between first person and RTS mode constantly, to place buildings After they're finished , which could kind of work if the AI wasn't completely useless,
If you leave your units alone, they'll shoot and follow whatever comes into range, meaning they may follow a damage enemy commander straight into tis base and suicide.
You could set them for guard mode, but that just means they'll stay in place and not engage at all.
Even if you play in full RTS mode, the unit pathfinding is clunky and your units tend to get murdered by the enemy commander and/or turrets because your units are having issues moving around obstacles.
The game needs work, specifically it needs a better system for constructing buildings, eg. queueing of buildings.
The AI also needs a lot of work, better pathfinding that also takes the units terrain and inter-unit hitbox into considering, better commands and better following of command; If i set units to guard mode, i want them to stay in place and rain hell on anything that gets into range.

I've now finished the game so i've updated my review.
This game is a lot of fun, not sure why the professional reviewers hate it so much. Maybe they're expecting it to be a fast-paced action game or something like that which it definitely isn't.
It's a detective game with an interesting story and characters that draws you in. It's also pretty novel in that you're playing a criminal-turned-detective's ghost who's trying to find the identity of his killer. You spend the game collecting clues to figure out your killer's identity while stopping along the way to help out other lost souls in little sidequests where you figure out how they died so they can pass on. There are also lots of collectibles, some of which provide background for the story, such as notes left by the main character's wife, or that unlock stories about unsolved crimes connected to hauntings. You end up collecting a lot of clues and you have to figure out which ones will help you solve whatever crime you're working on. They make sense and its fun. I've noticed a few negative reviews saying the clues don't make sense and you end up just clicking on everything till you get it right. I only did this once at the beginning of the game...and all I can say is, try thinking a bit and paying attention before just mashing your mouse. If you do this, you'll pretty quickly get a feel for how the clues work in the game and figure out which ones are useles. You can also posess the living, and while you can't move them, you can help them remember and eavesdrop on their conversations or thoughts. You can, however, posess cats which allow you to reach places you can't reach on your own. Everything about the game makes sense...you can't walk through the outdoor walls of buildings that have been consecrated, the demons you have to sneak past to take down from behind are souls who never passed on, etc. The mood the game sets just enhances the experience, being creepy and immersive.
Overall, this game is a lot of fun. Story is great, gameplay is fun, voice acting is well done. Having finished the game now, the story is a pretty good detective story, with everything falling satisfyingly into place at the end and a few neat twists. There are only a few drawbacks: the graphics aren't the best, but they're still decent (especially the lip synching); sometimes when you posess someone and listen to their thoughts you'll hear the same thought in different people; the parts where you have to sneak behind demons and take them out can be a bit tedious. However, all these are definitly worth overlooking.
The other drawback is that the game is a bit short. I finished it in 7 hours, and if you check out my achievements you'll see I didn't get 100% completion. I did all the side-quests and found as many collectibles as I could. You could probably stretch it out to 10 hours if you wanted 100% completion which seems totally possible in a single playthrough. Its up to you to decide whether a 7-10 hour game is worth $60 or if you want to wait for a sale.
In short, if you like story-driven games, or mystery/adventure games then you'll probably like this game. If you want this game to be a gritty shooter, then go buy Max Payne instead, because you won't get that with this game. Having finished it, I would now give it between a 7 and an 8 out of 10.
