There are few games that offer HUNDREDS of hours of gameplay that continue to be new and fun. Crusader Kings does this with gusto. Steam has me listed at 120 hours, this of course doesn't include the time I spent *ahem* trying it.

This game has a lot of potential but falls short numerous times on the mechanics which makes me unable to recommend it.
Take for example the slow motion feature which is implemented in such a way that with the same amount of fuel you can travel much much further depending on how much you want to slow down time. This means when you would normally need something like 2000 litres of fuel to reach the end you can do with just 500 litres if you play with the slow down time feature to the slowest option.
Also at random points during slow motion I would find that my fuel would not go down and I would not get any thrust yet I was holding down the thrust button and there were flames coming out of the thrusters (this continued even after I let go and press down again). At this point I forced to reset and hope nest time the same thing didn't happen or just play with slow motion off which ruins part of what makes this game unique. Also it is incredibly easy to fall though the ground if your going reasonably fast. As well as that I've had the game crash on me several occasions all of which have happened on "Astro lander" on the second planet.
The sandbox mode is fun but could be made better if co-op was added since there is such a big emphasis on weapons and ways to destroy things it would be great to use them against each other or to be able to help each other collect the stars around the map.
As for the good:
-The developer behind it seems very promising and I wouldn't be surprised to see him fix many of the issues listed above and maybe even adding suggestions others and I have had.
-The game has a very fair amount of content for the price so I doubt you'd feel ripped off for the price you'll pay (£6.99 is the standard price as of the day this review was put up).
-It has a great community of people who create really creative and different vehicles which is super easy to download for yourself to use.
However, as of today I personally feel as though this game is still in early access because of the numerous mechanical flaws. Hopefully one day I can update this review once the issues have been ironed out.

This is a game that i highly recommend for people that are into war games BUT NOT LIKE like call of duty and medal of honor this is game with swords and maces, axes, daggers and bows and old stuff... it will probably bug and lag sometimes but not too often. Its fun to play with friends very much, but when you are starting this game as a beginner you will probably die OFTEN... or not. (there are beginners that might be good or ok sometimes)
The games takes place back in the early 1400s and 1500s there are two teams: The Agatha knights and The Mason orders that are going to war, and everytime a new round starts you will get to chose between 4 classes: Archer, Man of arms, Vanguard and knight, and you can chose a lot of weapons to fight with OR if you are new you are forced to start with the basic weapons and everytime you kill or do actions you will get xp and points to get new ranks and new weapons. Each one of the classes has special abilities: The Archer can carry a portable shield around him and use it as cover, Man at arms can dodge if you press "v" while moving one direction, Vanguards can do sprint attacks (if you run long enough, the character will lift his weapon), The Knight will lose less stamina while blocking and has higher resistance to swing damage.
The combat system in this game is not too shabby at all you have three different attack-types: Poke, Slash and Overhead that you do attack with using the mouse and the mouse-scroll, the poke is for more reach and the overhead is for more damage plus slash is just a normal attack. You block with the right mouse-button and you can cancel an attack with the left mouse-button while starting an attack too.
There are different Game-types (objectives) in this game: Capture the flag,Team objective, Last team standing, Duel, King of hill and Free for all. Im not going to explain what you do in these... play it for yourself or watch videos on youtube about it.
This game is fun. well, at least the most fun-part is when you start the game and playing it with bots ...but when you start fighting the real pros of this game well, it might be F***ing hard and intense, it is too (i recommend you do the tutorial before you start the real game). They will often be Vanguards and Archers (but of course Knights and Man at arms too) you will die more often than getting more kills if you are starting or havent played in a while... but there comes that time when you are getting used to play the game and can play better than them... or like me NEVER. But you have to sit in many many hours practicing and playing so if you have a whole life to live dont do it.
I recommend this game very much but not the people under the age of 18. This game is very violent and contains blood and guts. And again... if you are looking for a gun-game dont chose this one then... or do it actually, because i am sure you will not be disappointed.

The difficulty and learning curve is steep at the beginning mostly due to adjusting to the controls. In order to perform a diagonal grapple you have to stand still. You can also do it by a diagonal push in that direction but because of it's small margin of detection on the stick half of the time it will either cause you to grapple up or horizontal. To chain grapple under a ceiling you have to push left or right. That's where I spent quite some time fighting my natural instinct to push diagonal.
Once you get used to the controls the difficulty plateaus a bit until you reach the final level, which turns out to be three times as big as any other area you've completed so far. Be sure to go back and collect lives because it can be really unforgiving.
With it's tendency to force players through trial and error gameplay such as "leap of faith" situations (there is no air control in this game) I can only recommend this to NES purist who were nostalgic of those long bygone days.

So many painful, horrible, awful decisions were made with this game.  Was there a real reason to use the PhsyX engine?  No.  Was there a reason for the terrible default keybindings?  Nope.  Was there a reason I am not allowed to shoot in any other direction than forward?  No!  Even with its issues, Bionic Commando (the 3D PC game) was actually a better game than this.  If you like games in the "forward shooting only" genre, then Broforce is a WAY better game, infinitely more satisfying, hilarious at times, and quite fun.  This game, however, needed a LOT more playtesting and polish before distributing it to the world.  Developers can learn this lesson:  I get they were trying to be relatively faithful to the original, but keep in mind those games were limited in what they could do because the hardware was limited.  Repeating janky controls from the original doesn't help matters in any way.  Buyer beware!  This game probably won't work on your hardware without modifications.  Namely you will have to hunt down the legacy PhysX engine, switch the game's executable to Windows 7 compatibility mode, and probably restart Steam like I did to get it to start without crashing.  This game wasn't received well by critics and now I know why.  It's an ill-conceived PC game - at best - and it hasn't aged well in the few years it has been out.

Warshift prides itself on being an RTS Game, also having features of an FPS Action game with RPG Elements, which is a very unique mix and in my opinion, makes this a great concept. This game implements the RPG Elements and FPS mode with one of its most important gameplay mechanics; Avatars.
An Avatar, on the Republic side, is a mechanised drone controlled by the commander (you) and offers a massive strategic advantage, to the point of being overpowered, giving you the ability to transform to either walk/drive, fly or submerge into the ocean. An Avatar can also hold four upgrades and five weapons. In my opinion, the upgrades system is gimmicky and as much as I know how to use it, it still seems like it can be improved. I have several suggestions on how the game can be improved but I know it's in Early Access and I can't wait for more content to be created by the one man developer, Cyril Megem. I am impressed but not surprised that this game is under development by a solo developer and as I'm hoping to aspire to the same level, I congratulate him on his achievements.
The story behind this game is, at the moment, quite bare, it only explains that Aliens, non-material beings, coming from the 'Gates of Chaos' can manipulate and control exoskeletons so they can impact the environment to their will. With this story, it makes two factions; the Alien Invaders and the Colonial Republic. Only having two factions doesn't offer much diversity but, again, I understand why this isn't possible as of yet; the developer, who is a graphic artist, game designer and programmer has to focus on developing the game, rather than expanding outwards just yet.
As far as the Real Time Strategy part of the game goes, it is very lackluster in my opinion, only having four maps, ten campaign missions and barely any units and buildings but I can understand why it may be lacking in these departments. Some of the missions objectives, at the start, weren't very clear and it's hard to get into at first. But once I did, after I finished the campaign at the highest difficulty, I just wanted more. The five hours I've already played have been nothing but pure enjoyment and I can see the potential this game has.
This game works very well on my Intel Core i3 computer, maintaining a very stable framerate at low quality settings because of my outdated graphics card. There is the occasional split-second freeze if there is a lot of pressure on my system but besides this, it should work very well on most, if not, all computers. The graphics are beautifully rendered but the engine and control could be optimised. The camera for the Raider Avatar was quite realistic but was no doubt, quite annoying, having to move my mouse back and fourth to get the right aim and lead to my death more than it should have.
Looking back on the game, to me, it was money very well spent and I'm glad to have shown my support. I can understand why some people might not be able to get into this game but for die-hard RTS and Action game fans, this is definitely a game to consider. I did not regret buying this game one bit and it was well worth it for me.

TL;DR: while it has a gorgeous art style, sublime soundtrack, and a highly creative concept, there's no overlooking the fact that the PC controls are pretty bad, the story is middling, and the voice acting is rather spotty at times. The overall experience makes me feel that the game was rushed out with a lot of it being left incomplete. (Which would explain its short running time.) I ended up never finishing the game because I encountered a bug, and didn't feel it was worth the frustration of fixing.
I wanted to love this game, and for the first 20 minutes or so I did. But now? Well, let's just say I am literally hoarse from screaming in frustration at how badly this game handles, at least with PC controls. I have no idea how it fairs on a controller, possibly that's the better avenue to go; I wouldn't know since I'm PC-exclusive and have no controller, nor a particular desire to use one.
What's so bad about the controls, you may ask? The character you play as, Dawn, is extremely finnicky to maneuver, especially in shadow form. (You know, the form she's in for ~90% of the platforming. Oh, what a delight.) Either she jumps a mile away from where you were aiming for or she only gets within inches of it. Either way: good luck nailing the desired landing spot without either backing up, having to start over from further back because you massively overshot, or with the use of a few extra hops forward to get you there. What makes this even worse is that you're often aiming for very narrow platforms, which means when you fall you fall out of shadow form and back into the real world. Typically this results in having to start that section ALL THE WAY OVER. I don't think I need to state how aggravating this is. When she's not in shadow form she navigates fine; the camera on the other hand does not. The mouse sensitivity when she walks is extremely low, yet for some reason when she runs it changes to about average sensitivity. Thankfully she runs automatically throughout most of the game, though there are a few instances where she walks and you can't force her to go faster, which is frustrating to say the least.
At one point you're introduced to a new mechanic, that being that you can break down more fragile objects in the 3D world by dashing through them. However, there's only a couple fences and three posts this ability can be used on, and no more. Were there more areas where this could be used planned initially but somehow didn't come to fruition? (A lot of this game feels like that: big plans that were never completed, whether due to budget issues or time constraints.)
I didn't really get a good feel for the game's world or lore, either. Now don't get me wrong, this game is dripping with atmosphere, but as far as how this world works, with the younger protagonist apparently being the only non-shadow person, I haven't a clue. There's lots of "collectibles" scattered around that provide information about things going on in the world, but most of them seem to be unrelated to the storyline, and as far as I could tell none of them really connect together. This results in a sense that the world was hastily put together, or that there was originally going to be a lot more content added to the game, but for some unknown reason was cut.
The characters aren't that great, either. The player protagonist, Dawn, has no character whatsoever. Didi, the second and unplayable protagonist, is a pretty average child character: nice, clever, just wants her family to stay together. It's clear that they try to make her funny and relatable by giving her lines that reference what would've been pop culture icons of the time period, but if anything this makes her seem blander since they're either quotes we've already heard before or revolve around things we're already quite familiar with. Sometimes they even come across as annoying, since the game seems to feel these references are much funnier than they really are. "Second star to the right and straight on 'til morning." Yay, you acknowledged Peter Pan exists after getting on a boat! A winner is you! Fortunately, these moments don't happen often. Actually the most interesting characters are her parents, Johnny and Kat, but we don't get to see them much at all. I wanted to know more about their past, what happened between them, what Johnny had been up to, and how Kat got her singing gig. Apparently the game decided that just wasn't interesting enough.
What did the game decide was more interesting instead? Having the pair of them fight to the point where Kat holds a gun to her head only to forgive Johnny, after he spouts one or two bland lines about how he can't live without his wife and daughter, and reunite with him less than a minute later! Yeah, the story in this game is sloppily put together, to say the least. That moment alone captures one of the game's main problems: it clearly wants to get an emotional reaction out of you, but this moment of conflict was resolved so quickly that none was earned, and so none was given. It's all too rushed, there aren't enough scenes to build these characters, so we, the players, don't get to have any kind of relationship with them. They're acquaintences, we know almost nothing about any of them, which makes it impossible to really care about their struggles.
Speaking of the parents: the voice acting from everyone else in the game is fine; nothing outstanding, but perfectly serviceable. The parents however? They come across as forced and somewhat wooden in their deliveries. I never once bought any real emotion from them. I feel like they were definitely trying for real emotion, but just never quite managed to land it. Fortunately, you don't have to deal with them for more than a third of the game, so this is a nitpick I guess.
The story itself promises some really interesting points, like hinting that perhaps Dawn pulled Didi out of the shadow form and into a 3D form, the way Dawn can do this with items she holds. But it's never explained how this power works or even where it came from, and the story ends on that note making this question doubly frustrating. I don't know if this was left open in the hopes of a sequel, but there doesn't appear to be one coming anytime soon, so I guess we'll never know.
I did say at the start that I encountered a bug that didn't allow me to finish, so the only reason I know about the cliffhanger ending is because I watched a playthrough on YouTube. The bug I encountered was that I was unable to make a certain dash, no matter what I did I always fell out of shadow form, and after ~20 tries I gave up. The game had already stopped being fun for about an hour before that point and felt too much like work, so I couldn't even be bothered to find a fix or post a forum discussion about it. The only reason I've clocked in over 2 hours at all was because I was desperately hoping that if I pushed forward I would manage to get to a point where some of the charm from the beginning would return. (Hint: it didn't.)
So what is there to like about this game? Well, as I mentioned before, it does have a very pretty art style and a good atmosphere and soundtrack. It also runs okay on average-to-lower end PCs. The concept itself is a good one as well, though truth be told I don't feel it was explored to its full potential. Are these small, good bits enough to make up for its otherwise lackluster performance? In my opinion: no. However, I guess I can't go so far as to say, "This game should be avoided at all costs, don't ever play it."
In short: if you're into platformers and very, very forgiving, then I guess I'd hesitantly recommend trying it the next time it goes on sale, if you have a console. (Again: possibly the game handles better with a controller instead of a keyboard and mouse.) But for the rest of you: if you've only got a PC, skip it and go play Portal instead.

As I expected, the second game in the Bioshock franchise delivered a very similar experiance to the first game. Only this time, you were returning to Rapture as a seasoned veteren, as opposed to new player who has never seen the likes of this atmospheric game before. Which all in all is not a bad thing if you've never played Bioshock before, but if you've already played though the entire first game (like myself) then you may find this instalment lacking in creative content.
That isin't to say that Bioshock 2 dosen't bring new elements to the franchise. You play as a Big Daddy, but you still get to use plasmids, which does make combat incredibly fun. No more wrench, now you have a drill. No more pistol, now you finally have one of those Rivet guns that you could never pick up or use in the first game. However, as a big Daddy you can now accompany little sisters on their harvests for extra Atom, only to either harvest or save them by the end.
Bioshock 2 Remastered also comes with the Minerva's Den DLC, which I highly reccomend. It gives that Bioshock itch a good scratch by staying true to the Bioshock formula of having a mysterious plot and twist ending, but also introducing a new Big Daddy and a lovely new gun to fight it with.
Bioshock 2 also introduces new enimes, like Brut Splicers, Big Sisters and a couple new Big Daddies. However in the end, a few small changes are not enough to make Bioshock 2 better the then first Bioshock game. It just dosen't have the same sense of wonder and mystery that made the first game so great. Does that mean Bioshock 2 is by any means a bad game? No. That would be like saying a 8/10 game is bad just because the previouse game was a 9/10.
So do I think Bioshock 2 is better the the first Bioshock? No, I do not. Do I think you should still play it? Absolutely, It is still an engaging, enjoyable and well made FPS that is much better then so many other games on the market.

Being only Early Access I can't fairly "Not Recommend" this game but for those looking for some insight from people who've purchased and played a little, read on:
From the very start, the current campaign is only half the size you would expect from that of an epic RTS. All levels are open so there's really no sense of progress. Everything is served up like a sampling tray. Skirmishes are limited to only a few maps and the map designs constrain tactics so there are only a few various approaches that would be effective or practical.
Also to clarify you can not take direct control of any unit. The only unit you have direct control of is your hero from which there is a selection of three or four for either of Warshift's two factions.  A keyboard/mouse AND gamepad combonation is highly recommended to have on hand to quickly fumble back and forth between.
On the plus side the concept is solid and so is the eye-candy. Giving the small one man team the game play is reasonably good even at this time despite tactical options being constipated respective of map designs.
To me this ultimately looks like a prototype sampler for larger development houses like EA or Ubisoft to pick up and run with, doubling the size of the campaign, adding more factions, tacking on fancy voice-worked FMVs and locking away the levels so the whole story isn't spilled out from the start.
If such turns out to be the case I don't mind the $15 I've spent so far as long as there is going to be a fat discount for supporters if Warshift does, indeed, take the route that Toy Soldiers did.

DISCLAIMER: the 'does not recommend' is for the remaster, not the original. "Bioshock 2" is a phenomenal game. The remaster is terrible due to technical failings.
A beautiful, crashtastic mess. Even with the recommended fixes, the aptly named 'RemasTURD' is still an unstable pile of you-know-what. Which is frustrating, because when it's actually running, the graphics are lovely and the game play is engaging. The crashes were completely unpredictable. Sometimes, it would be hours between crashes. Sometimes, the game would crash three or four times in a row.  It would hapen in combat, out of combat, immediately following loads, during saves, in the middle of an empty hall. In areas that were graphically intense or places that had few textures or animation. Places with no enemies at all, places with only one enemy that had yet to activate/become hostile. The best way to circumvent loss of progress was to save frequently, but having to save every few minutes does more than ruin immersion. It turns into a chore what should be a good, clean fun.
"Bioshock 2" is a great game, but suffers from both kinds of 'sequel syndrome.' Firstly, it's predecessor was so innovative and successful that one can't help but have expectations for this installment, which inevitably leads to disappointment. Secondly, it can't quite step out of the previous game's shadow in the story department, at least as far as plot is concerned. Simple plot summary: the player assumes the role of someone who arrives unexpectedly (and mysteriously), with unknown motivations. The player receives immediate assistance via radio from a person of influence. This ally convinces the player they are both on the same side and should unite against a common enemy... who happens to be the person running the city. Sound familiar?
This installment seems to place greater focus on new game play elements and encounters (Big Sisters, a greater selection of Gene Tonics and more available slots, a different mini-game for hacking, etc). Options on how to manage Little Sisters are more interesting (harvest? gather? rescue?) and the new plasmids make for intriguing changes in play (Scout is a lot of fun, especially for those who enjoy stealth/infiltration games). The new weapons are enjoyable, as well (even if some were functionally indentical to their counterparts in the first game, they still have a unique look and feel).
Atmospherically, the music is... off. It's hard to describe, but in comparison to the first game, the placement, prominence and selection of music in "Bioshock 2" just doesn't feel up to snuff. In "Bioshock," the music was superb. The right track playing at just the right time to maximize mood and effect not only enhanced the game, but enriched it. "Bioshock 2" has another great soundtrack, but it's not implemented anywhere near as well. Memorable tracks that are representative of the era in which the game is set and are thematically appropriate seem to be arranged in an almost forgettable manner and are often subverted by ambient sound effects (even after adjusting music and SFX volumes in the audio options menu). Sad.
8/10 for the story, new design elements and continued development of the game world. The original version of "Bioshock 2", if stable, is recommended unconditionally. As is, the "RemasTURD" is an experience to be endured rather than enjoyed.

~~My first review~~
Let me first explain my negative review. Ultimately, I wouldn't recommend this game to myself. Rather, I would recommend Dustforce to masochists, personal enemies, and professional platform gamers.
I really wanted to like Dustforce. The promo videos made it seem like one casually 'ninjas' and floats about beautiful 16 bit levels collecting cobwebs like Sonic collects rings. Not quite.
The concept itself is interesting. The goal is to travel through obstical courses as fast as possible. Along the way, you must run through patches of dust and hit "enemies" in order to clear the level. This is a 2D speed-running game.
The physics and mechanics make absolutely no sense to the uninitiated casual game playing plebian like myself. It can be frustrating, repetative and time consuming simply jumping from platform to platform in the overworld. This is where you wander around finding doors to unlock, which represent individual levels.
Compare with titles like Super Meat Boy and Cave Story. These games present challenging and interesting game play, while having control schemes and movement that are predictable and intuitive. Dustforce DX creates simple levels, that are made challenging by a character that is difficult to control. Essentially, they took a relatively simple concept and made it difficult to enjoy on account of sloppy, tendinitis aggravating controls that are frustrating to learn and maddening to master.
Further, the actual levels are fairly uninteresting and easy to get through. The challenge is that in order to properly complete a level, simply getting through it is not enough. You need to get the fastest time possible without missing any dust. This means repeating levels until you have every move perfected. This ends up being more busy work than anything else. You could easily spend a thousand hours trying to perfect each level. Combined with controls that assault your hands, it can be a very unforgiving process of which I quickly grew tired.
I suppose in the Genre of repetitive games which slap you around and demand perfection it succeeds. However, I guess I'm not a fan of games where developers decided the best way to make a game challenging is to make the character barely controllable. I feel like back in the days of original 8 bit graphic platformers, this would simply be called bad controls and it would be relegated to 2 and 3 star reviews. These days there are gamers who specifically enjoy and excel at games with lousy controls, and I suspect if you're one of those people you will find a lot of fun in spending countless hours punishing yourself on Dustforce.
Recall the viral flash game where the object is to control a sprinters limbs to push him over the finish line, or rather see how far you can comically stumble and hobble across a track. This is the same concept taken to it's inevitable extreme...
OK, it's not THAT bad, but you'll be spending a half hour trying to jump onto a ledge just to get to another stage... only to discover that you don't have the key to unlock it. Oh right, keys.
In order to unlock all the levels, you will need to complete the stages with perfect scores to accumulate keys. Ugh.
Summary;
If you are considering using the standard keyboard layout, either get an ice pack for your hands or forget about it. The game is barely playable on a game-pad, which is far superior to the keyboard controls.
If you're a demi-god with spaghetti fingers and the ability to pick up outrageous controls, and have a lot of time and patience, I guess you will LOVE this game.
If you're a casual gamer who likes simple controls, and doesn't want to invest the hours it will take to teach your hands to waltz like noodles through endlessly repetitive levels of dust ninja then get Super Meat Boy instead.

The amount of satisfaction you gain when you do something like that is astounding in the sense that even after 300+ hours on the game that feeling never seems to cease giving the high of happines every time.
Section 3:Picking the right settings
Ark runs well and smooth, adding mods or turning the graphics to high can create FPS lag which creates a negative experience. If you have a supercomputer then plan to use the epic settings which is the best possible graphics setting in ark. im going to list the graphics settings but not give a descroption like the one above for fear of hate. The graphic are going from highest to lowest, the settings include Epic, High, Medium, Low.
Section 4:Ending words

I'm not going to cover many points that have already been covered by many other reviewers in great depth - today I'm only covering 1: "Pay to win" or microtransactions.
I am over 500 hours into this game I have not spent any money at all and have a plethora of items. Many items I have acquired in-game by running void relic missions and it usually takes me about 5-10 missions to get the relics I need to build a new frame. In this time I also acquire a few spare parts which I save up and either trade in for ducats (another currency) which can be used to buy rare items ever 2 weeks from a vendor known as Baro Kiteer, or I go to the warframe market website and place on there to gain platinum.
Example. I went on a Sortie mission the other day and won an "unveiled shotgun riven mod" after about 15 minutes of gameplay. I don't use shotguns and I was still not high lvl to use the tigris, so I sold it..... for 140 platinum. I did a few void missions and later that evening I had spare parts to sell a "full vauban prime set" which went for 110 platinum. I used this to buy more slots for my inventory and a "nova prime" frame (vaulted, meaning it cannot be won in game anymore).
You cannot spend 20-30 hours in this game and expect to win the best items.
You cannot spend 20-30 hours in this game and expect to drop enough items to sell, to buy the best items.
But if you enjoy the game, the missions, the community, the different playstyles of the frames and the different weapons, then that act of just playing nets you all the items and platinum you could ever need.
With regards to the time spent on building the blueprints: 12 hours of build time is nothing seeing as Im at work when most items are building, ready for me to collect when I get home. 72 hours to build a new warframe is nothing when you consider that while its building you can get other weapons and unlock new stories and missions and level up what you currently have. I think many people expect instant gratification for free, but of course this is where DE makes the money - some people are so impatient that they will throw hundreds at this game, but if I was a developer and people where willing to throw their money at me then Id accept it too.
TL;DR:
If you enjoy the game and what you get for free then a little patience gets you nearly everything you want... for free. I have been playing a few hours a night for a month now and Ive unlocked 50% of all frames (including vaulted).
Looking at this review now, and seeing the amount of entertainment Ive got for the cost of Zilch... I actually feel guilty

I have to say, I'm very impressed with this alpha.
I have some minoristic experience with the previous game crashing on my dads Xbone and getting cremed by a fire demon, and I have to say that coming to this game off of that one is suprisingly refreshing. The whole game is built up off of the original Dungeons and Dragons games like Baulders Gate, or if not it's errily similar. But the game has less complexities making it a good choice for bot veterans and new players. It is an old game brought to the new age like it should be.
The game is real time while roaming the world but follows a turn based battle progression when you engage an enemy. Something interesting is the emphisis on enviorment and using your surroundings and gear to keep your foe in check. Attacks will honour line of sight and can hit a wall if you don't check the pathing of the attack. This applys to your foes as well, and with the plethora of effects and options, this game will test your stradigizing more than your endurance.
But let that serve as a warning, too. Unless you're willing to invest the time into the game, you won't be going very far. There are no safety rails or training wheels. You will be placed at the mercy of the world with only your wits to keep you safe. There is value in every gold coin you can find, and armour isn't so expendable. This creates a unique value to everything you can procure, and leaves the final decision down to you whether your ready or not.
This is a stradigy game in every sense of the word. And it's damn worth it. I alone sunk roughly 30 hours into what's avalibe here,
, and I didn't run into many bugs, which is suprising for an alpha. I'm very much looking forward to the complete game and, heck, even more of the alpha and inevitable beta.

The beginning of this game is quite enjoyable. The tone of the story is amusing, the gameplay is engaging, and the card-based mechanic is easy to pick up and fun to use.
As the game goes on, however, it becomes more and more luck based. Will you get the loot that will enable you to win? Will you draw the right card at the right time? While there is a degree of skill here, the amount of times that you die because a character receives an involuntary trait that you don't want, or simply doesn't receive relevant equipment drops and gets slaughtered by monsters for having a deck that doesn't mesh well with their core strengths makes the late game more frustrating than fun.
If they included any features that allowed for deck tuning (disabling certain equipment, for instance, or being allowed to pick traits) this could be mitigated somewhat. But they don't. So the end game is basically watching characters die repeatedly until one gets lucky enough with their first few encounters to be able to carry a dungeon handily.

I loved playing L.A. Noire. The homicide desk is my favorite. It stays true to old-school noir-style storytelling while using advanced technology that places real actors' faces and facial expressions in the game. The story is compelling (this is a narrative game as opposed to a choices matter game; even though I prefer the latter, I did not mind that this game was the former- I think it worked better this way), the character designs are out of this world thanks to the motion camera technology, and the world is accurate to 1940s Los Angeles and beautiful (albeit for show and not really filled with content outside of the cases and collectibles). I was really immersed into the detective work and the lie detection system (which is the main gameplay, although there is also car chases, shootouts, brawling, and more!).
It took me thirty and a half hours to complete the main game (including DLC), but another almost fifteen hours to get 100% completion. My only wish is that Rockstar would follow their original plans of making the "Noir" games a series of games. I would buy LA/NY/Chicago/etc Noire 2 in a heartbeat even if it did not feature the original characters (who I also enjoyed getting to know/ controlling).

Dragon Age: Inquisition was a huge AAA title, and frankly, it only surpasss the original game in term of scale. I purchased DA:I and this early access game at the same time, I played DA:I for 30 minute, it was meh. The graphic on the PC port was disastrous, but that wasnt the problem, but the borring combat, where you spam skills, wait for cooldown, then spam again. The first act of DOS II swallowed 20 hours of my time, and it was a sliver of what it would be when it is released.
Every battle in the original DOS is a sandbox for you to play, every decision made brings about countless outcome and possibility. A powerful spell can bring about destruction on both party, and environment awareness is thrown into that mix, it was the gist of the first DOS.
DOS II bring that to a whole level, every surface can be manipulated with bless or curse, bringing two other layers of gameplay for each element. If you stand in a blessed fire you are immune to burn and heal, as opposed to cursed fire which hurts you even more and cannot be removed.
Then we have elevation and mobility. The game gives bonus and penalty for being on higher and lower ground, respectively, as well as new moves that can teleport you to around the battle field. Movement is no longer sluggish like the original game.
And finally, the biggest improvement is Magic Armor and Physical Armor. Every entity in the game has two types of defense, so you have to break the Magic Armor before you can damage their HP with Magic, and vice versa. Armor also help you defend against status and crown control as long as your armor toward that type of damage isnt broken (ie you cannot be burned unless your Magic Armor is at 0 and you cannot be knocked down unless your Physical Armor is broken). This encourage you do diversify your party and build, while keeping you on your toe. Mages have weak Physical armor but strong Magic armor, the opposite is true with Tanks and Rogue/ Ranger stands in between. So you will always want to exploit your surrounding, keep your Mage out of their tank, Keep your tank in their mage's face. The combat starts out slow, but wraps up quickly.
Once you grasp the full extend of these changes, the game is very enjoyable. It was fun enough to let me look pass the technical issue, bugs and lacking assets like voice over and music. After all, this is an early release version.

A FANTASTIC game.....
.....if you can run it. This game badly needs a patch cause getting it to run consists of downloading old NVIDIA drivers. It doesn't overwrite your current drivers, though. It just uses them for this game rather than newer ones, which is weird. I don't know whether I should recommend it or not when it's such a good game but such a bad port. Port aspect aside, and considering that there was a solution for it (unlike the Sam and Max games), let's move onto the game itself:
[✔] Challenging AND fair
[✔] Creative use of unique game mechanics
[✔] Doesn't try to be an ''interactive experience''
[✔] Good music and Presentation
After playing The Tomb Raider reboot and Bioshock Infinite this game was a Godsend. Like The Swapper, there's a unique game mechanic (the hook) and the game makes creative use of it throughout. Most boss fights are you entering a room and having to figure out how to use your hook to defeat them. The game doesn't throw hints if you don't get it in 10 seconds and it's always a rational process of deduction.
Not having a jump button might seem really odd at first, but after a few hours you wouldn't have it any other way. The shooting is of the Megaman variety, albeit less varied. This is more of a platformer and the enemies' bullets serve more as obstacles to platforming rather than the main challenge itself.
Wish the second one was on Steam, although I hear that game sucked♥♥♥♥♥and they added a jump mechanic.
It's worth noting that the guy behind the Payday Soundtracks did the OST for this game, and it shows ✔

Bionic Commando Rearmed é um relançamento da CAPCOM. O jogo original foi lançado em 1987 e, francamente, era muito mais legal que essa versão nova.
Link do vídeo no 40 jogados:
O jogo é do gênero aventura/ação em duas dimensões,  onde você assume o comando de um soldado cuja missão é resgatar um outro soldado que aparentemente está sendo mantido refém de um grupo terrorista, além de ter que descobrir tudo o que puder sobre o tal grupo.
A jogabilidade é bem ruim, os comandos são pouco funcionais e o pior de tudo é que o personagem é grudado no chão. Ele não consegue ultrapassar nem uma caixa de sapatos sem utilizar seu gancho, o que é, no mínimo, incoerente. Os gráficos são bons, mas não chegam a salvar o jogo e a história é "clichezaça" ao máximo.

In terms of number of different units and buildings - it's a pretty simple game, even more simple than Starcraft. But in terms of multiplayer fun, it's extremely fun. One player on each team is the commander and creates all the normal units and buildings. The second and third players on each team focus entirely on their combat avatars, and play a third-person action game where they can turn the tide of battle, and are required to activate energy points so that the commanders can place more buildings.
Think of it as an action MOBA where you have a lot more control over the buildings and units on the battlefield. Or, think of it as a simplified version of what Starcraft Ghost could have been.

This game is too broken to enjoy sadly. Even if you think you're the cats meow when it comes to troubleshooting you won't get this going and I'd bet money on that. However if you fancy the challange and are still interested after that warning then I'll leave some Pros and Cons for the game itself.
Pros
-It feels like good old Bioshock, which for me is the biggest draw
-The new areas of Rapture are full of detail and show a side to rapture we never saw in the original
-The new weapons are well designed with more upgrades than the original, however 1 less weapon overall
-Adam is earned more often and I felt like I put it to better use than in the original
-I find this game to be the perfect length, it ended and I didn't yearn for more nor was a bored by that point
-The individual character stories are amazing, the detail is insane and deciding the fate of some of the big players in rapture leads to some very entertaining storylines
-The combat is great, bit more action based than the original but it works well for the game.
Cons
-Overall the story is lacking substance and is very cheesy when talking about Elanor and Lamb.
-The crashes of course, I must of restarted at least 30 times, with patches and fixes in place, SAVE REGULARLY!
-The FOV is very broken often the camera clips into the body, as well as the stupid big daddy helmet border
-The little sister gathering protection side quests were so dull, I did a few then but just ended up skipping them entirely
-The difficulty scaling is dreadful. The start is far too difficult on Normal and Hard and the end is far too easy on Normal and Hard
-It's not scary, at all. Bioshock had some creepy locals and jumpscares but this has, literally nothing.
-I hated the new video based research camera and the new hacking was too basic.
-There's too much money and resources, I could just ignore some of the weaker weapons, especially my drill, which is a bit silly considering how devestating is should be
-Some Achievements are broken, this was a bit irritating, I wouldn't of got them all but I'd of liked the ones for the tasks I'd completed
-The remaster doesn't include the multiplayer
Honestly, if you have the patience this is a great game. Everyone has a different expirience but my crashes were plentiful and aggrivating. While I enjoyed the game, I spent far too much time relaunching it and backtracking over areas I'd done but not had the chance to save at before crashing. I want to get immersed but I'll forget to save and vice versa. As much as I do love this game, if it wasn't for the fact that I'm playing all 3 games in order, I'd of not played this at all.

is a rated Mature run-and-gun side-scrolling platformer very similar to
. The primary characteristic alike in both of these games is the ability only to swing from area to area instead of including a button to jump. I know that many children and teenagers growing up won’t be able to appreciate this remake of the classic Nintendo Entertainment System game because it already seems to hard without a jump button. I do realize wholeheartedly the stigma that would♥♥♥♥♥♥modern-day gamers off. I understand you, but I assure you if you have some time, patience and practice, then you will get good at this game and succeed. One of the main hallmarks in the
and the
series is action-packed run-and-gun gameplay that shows no mercy toward enemies.

The graphics have been updated from the original Nintendo Entertainment System counter-part. They are now more crisp, show improved lighting and have a better enemy, environment animations. The story is presented through communication hubs that tell you more about the story as you progress through the levels. The story is the classic hallmark of many real-life warzone tales and stories of today.
The primary characteristic that sets
and
apart from many platformers now is that they can be played in a variety of ways. If you are really good already at the game, you can choose to speedrun while skipping the story and many enemies. You don’t always have to take on every single enemy; this is all up to you based on how much health you currently have and how well you trust in your skills. Unlike some platformers that require only button pressing to be successful,
requires you to know enemy patterns precisely; Capcom did this within the original Mega Man games as well. If your movement is even the slightest bit unprecise, you are going to have to replay levels again and again until you clear them.
In fact, I remember watching some gamers on the REACT YouTube channel play the original
on the original Nintendo and they struggled. The difference there was that
allowed for extra continues. However,
does not have that feature. Either you occasionally gain extra lives from level to level and refill more health by defeating random enemies, or you have one life to make the most of it.
Yes, and no. If you are a modern-day gamer that wants a trip back through nostalgia and have never played the old-school side-scrolling hard platformers that were around back then, this will give you a first-person test-drive through all those years, in the late 1980’s through early 1990’s. However, if you are like me and don’t have as much time as you used to right now to play games and not enough patience or time before moving on to other games in your backlog, then I would not recommend it. However, if you don’t have a fairly large backlog and want something to play for a long while, constantly improving and transitioning between all the difficulties from easy to hard.
You use basic mechanics on the keyboard while using the arrow keys also to control your release of your bionic arm. You need precise aim to be able to swing and pull yourself up to other platforms. This is the hallmark of these original side-scrolling games like this. The controls work ok for keyboard and mouse, but I know I am not alone when I say that the original experience is much better through using a controller. It would be awesome if there could be PC compatibility for a Nintendo Entertainment System controller.
•Awesome 8-bit soundtrack that is high action
•Awesome main character model that has been updated from the original. The main character looks cooler than he did before
•Enemy models are represented based on their colors by faction
•It is fun to run-and-gun and shoot enemies that we need to kill for a purpose
•Excellent objectives, goals and milestones to work towards
•Might not appeal to the current generation of gamers we currently have
•Takes much time and patience since there is also one initial life without any continues in single-player
•More variety of controller options would be a nice addition for Capcom to add eventually
•Capcom, give us a remastered version of the 2008 more current generation version to go along with this one
A good remake of a classic side-scrolling platformer that takes strategy, time and patience to master.

Bionic Commando for the NES, to this day, is still my all time favourite NES game. When I learned they were going to do a remake a couple of years ago I got really excited and in the end, all of my expectations were met. They did everything right!
This game keeps the original game intact while building off it, minor adjustments to some of the level design and adding a couple of gameplay mechanics like barrel grabbing and Interactive Wiretap Hacking. It is a true remake done well in a day and age where remakes and remasters tend to be used as quick cash grabs, leeching of the previous gaming gen for cheap and easy work. The graphics look really nice and polished and many new visual details have been added to the game including great lighing effects that really add a great level of atmosphere and even the music has been kept intact but giving it this nice current day techno style remix vibe update.
My favourite part was always the fact that you couldn't jump and had to rely on your swinging skills from your bionical arm, it's a game that truly relies on your skill to master the swinging as it can be pretty technical, letting go in time, short swings, reeling in and letting go on time while continuesly swinging about. The overhead stages have been remade as well and were kept in the game and I love it how you have more control now making them a lot more fun to go through compared to its NES counter part were they become more of a hindrance, a chore.
All in all, even if you never experienced the original NES game, this remake can truly hold its own, great gameplay, nice looking graphics, an impressive soundtrack, a cool story and most of all, just pure fun.
For a couple of comparisons with the old game check out this video here where I talk about Remakes done right, Bionic Commando and Binic Commando Rearmed being my prime examples:

If a game is awkward and unintuitive by design, can I really fault it? And am I prepared to be lynched for it?
Yes, also yes.
I actually played this years ago on the Xbox 360, and remembered having a lot of trouble acclimating to the controls. I thought for sure that I was just a dumb kid back then, and that I'd get it the second time as a big strong adult. I sucked at platforms back then, and retro inspired ones especially. Now I'm a Castlevania fan. Times have changed! And this is a universally praised platformer, held higher than it's 2008 fully 3D remake, and I loved that game to death. I have to give it another try. It couldn't be as awkward as I remember.
It was just as awkward, and I'll attempt to somehow explain.
Imagine you were playing Metroid. You move, you shoot, you hop on platforms, pits are instant death, and touching enemies boops ya away. Now remove jumping. Now have all movement controls mapped to combinations of directions on the left control stick and the B button.
Not so hard, right? Now make sure almost none of that directional input is the direction you want to go. Going upwards is about the only thing you're getting into your muscle memory without a fight. Simple actions requires unintuitive commands, such as pressing down and B to pull yourself under a gap to the left or right, or pressing B with no directional input to swing to the left or the right. This might not sound like too much, but when levels are multiple tiers of platforms full of enemies and death pits, it can be really frustrating to try and pull off multiple different kinds of obtuse commands and keep it all straight in your head.
No one move you pull off is particularly complicated or outlandish, it just defies muscle memory with it's obtuse commands.
So when everything is built around this bizarre 45 degree angle flat plain traversal, what am I to do when the first boss required me to interacting with something that was an inch off the ground? Yep. That's what did me in. That was what made me quit. A slightly raised barrel convinced me to refund Woolies Sacred Cow and then come to ♥♥♥♥♥ about how it's totes overrated yo.

Really charming little story-driven game with a stylish 1920s-meets-Coraline aesthetic. The shadow platforming mechanics can be really finicky, but the game is short enough that I didn't really have time to be too frustrated with it (I completed the game in just shy of 3 hours). It doesn't hurt that the game's story is compelling... a point of comparison might be The Unfinished Swan, in that the mechanics of the game wouldn't hold my interest on their own but work well within the narrative.
I went in a little nervous because a lot of reviews mention the game being buggy. I played on PC and did not encounter any bugs.

This is a cutesy, albeit short, puzzle game. I did finish the game in about 3 hours and I did spend some time searching for collectibles. I don't think there is much in terms of replayability.
The story itself seems at times heavy enough to be aimed at adults, but the way the story is told makes me believe the authors of the game intended it to be played by children. There are some pretty big things that are not explained about the world such as "Why are the edges of the playable world a twisted void?". The story in this game broaches the subject of
, but the game also contains violence
. If you intend to let a kid play this game, I would recommend playing through it yourself once.
The core mechanic (shifting in and out of shadow mode) feels fun and the puzzles you can solve with it are reasonably varied. I didn't find the puzzles very difficult, but some of them did require some out-of-the-box thinking. While exploring for luminaries and other collectibles I found that I did run into random invisible walls quite a bit. The movement in the game sometimes feels a bit glitchy, but you can open shortcuts along the way, allowing you to quickly retry something that did not go well, so I feel this is not really a big deal.
: The world you walk, jump and shift around in feels interesting. Some of the music in the game is quite good. The rest of it does at least not feel repetitive to me. The voice-acting is a mixed bag, but it could have been much worse.
Overall I would say that the game is worth a try.

I stumbled across this game through my enthusiastic following of the developers’ other work We Happy Few. Contrast brings the same dark, yet refreshing feel. The developers were not afraid to take risks. The gameplay greatly fed into a narrative which I obsessed over until the end. The 3D to 2D platforming mechanic allowed for interesting and uniquely thought-provoking puzzles. The design of the shadows in this game was simply stunning; as was the rest of the game. The art team truly created masterpieces in the beautiful, immersive world. Not only is the game visually beautiful, the sound track is truly amazing, and the voice actors were phenomenal. There were some areas which seemed buggy, and the final puzzles differed greatly from the rest of the game. This did lead to a few steps which almost stumped me. The combination of a thrilling story, gorgeous visuals, gorgeous music and voice acting, and thought-provoking and addictive puzzle-platformer mechanics is a winning combination which I would willingly play for hours on end. And this is the games only obstacle: it is INCREDIBLY short. Missing only 5 of the in-game collectables, I completed the storyline in under 4 hours. The developers created a world which I would LOVE to spend days in. The story ended so quickly, that I am amazed at how phenomenal the characters were able to be developed.  I would love to see this universe expanded upon. Not factoring in price, I would highly recommend this game any day. That being said, sadly, I do not feel this game has much replay value. Again, however, as a refreshing take on a puzzle-platformer, I love the work these developers put into this game. It could have potentially been one of my favorite games I’ve played in the past 10 years, if it only had even a few more chapters to it. Still, it is definitely worth checking out, especially if it ever goes on sale.

A non-biased quick look @ the game:
Impressive in both scope and visual quality this space epic combines Action, RTS and RPG elements. You can build bases, manage armies, and then come down to keep the enemies at gunpoint, gain experience in dynamic battles and customize your main characters or vehicles.
In 2062, the colonial planet “Enigma” was invaded by an aggressive alien race Atroid’s from the parallel world that has gone into our universe through the hypothetical “Gates of Chaos”. This non-material beings were forced to clothe their energy nucleuses in the strong physical shells (exoskeletons), as they needed to have impact on the environment in our world. As a result, they created an army of alien droids which are capable to fight in any environment and at any temperature. The fortifications of the planetary defense line turned out to be not effective against the powerful energy weapon used by the aliens. Soon, the biosphere of the planet felt the destructive power of their deadly attack, and a half of its surface turned into a lifeless desert. The miner colony garrison that was made up of volunteer soldiers suffered huge losses and was urgently evacuated. All resource extraction works on the planet were suspended, and corporations began to bear huge losses. But, after numerous antiwar protests, the government of the Colonial Republic did not want to risk human lives, and scientists had to create an entirely new army of intergalactic operations. The republican fleet and the assault battalion “Delta”, consisting of cyber-guards, heavy machinery and robotic drones-transformers was sent to the planet. The Commanders who have telepathic skills control that steel armada while being aboard the ARKS. For the purpose of their own safety, they are forbidden to leave the ARK. However, they can be directly involved in battles as operators of combat avatars (unmanned combat robotic vehicle). - Recommended!

WARSHIFT:
~~~~~~~~~
The planet Enigma has been invaded by the Atroid’s, an alien race who came from a parallel world with a tendency, shall we say… towards hostility! On board the ARK (assault ship), you will telepathically command an army of cyborg guards, droids and heavy Machinery, and mount your counter attack against the invaders.
Warshift is a very interesting game, merging RTS and 3rd person action games. At the start of each mission, you will be briefed on your objectives via a video, then you will be in the ARK hangar and you will be presented with your combat avatar (the unit that you will control when you jump to the 3rd person view) and have the opportunity to add weapons and upgrades.
For the gameplay aspect, you will have to build structures to drill resources, AI cyborgs base, AI vehicle base and gun platforms to defend the ARK and other structures. Every 60 seconds, new units will appear from the relevant base (if built) automatically. At any given time you can swap from a RTS gameplay to a 3rd person and take command of your combat avatar. If you are like me, it will take you a while to get used to it and it can be frustrating at time.
The current version of WARSHIFT has a campaign mode with 10 missions, a Skirmish and multiplayer mode. The graphics are really good and the game runs well. In terms of the controls, for the 3rd person point of view it is fine but I feel the camera when you play RTS aspect needs to be better (need to be faster when zooming in and out).
I am very impressed by the fact that this project has being developed by only one person!
Positives:

-	Good and polished graphics
-	Intriguing gameplay
-	Runs well
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	A tad difficult to master and can become frustrating
-	No achievements at this stage
-	No trading cards at this stage
This game has great potential, have a look at it!

Warshift is a cool blend between a shooter and real-time strategy game.
The game doesn't have much depth in AI units. For example, you can't build a tonne of different types of units and upgrading them multiple times like in other strategy games. However, the game makes up for that with the ability to directly control one of your units. You can choose between a handful of units to control, which all play differently. These units have unique weapons, and have different abilities. These controllable units can also be upgraded.
The maps are pretty cool, with a decent variety. You also have the ability to customize all sorts of traits such as the weather, and where everyones units spawn on the map in a skirmish mode.
There's also a campaign which gives you a set battlefield depending on what mission you choose, and certain objectives to complete.
It's a nice breath of fresh air to the strategy genre that I personally feel has become a bit stale over time. This isn't the most amazing, innovative strategy game, but it's decent fun and worth a look!

Great game. The first has become a favorite of mine and this one seems to be improving upon in in a lot of ways. However, there are a few things that I think could use some work. As this is an early access game, I truly hope that the Dev's are looking into these reviews. I have no idea how to give them constructive criticism outside of this forum. I guess I will try their website next.
My issues: The new armor system is an awesome addition. It changes battle strategy in amazing ways. However, it is truly unfortunate that no status effects can be given to anyone who still has even a sliver of corresponding armour. This ruins the early battle efficiency of a number of spells and abilities, and unless you spend time wittling each enemies armour down before killing them off (a terrible tactical plan) most AOE skills (namely spells) have very little value. My suggestion to fix this would be to have each point in an armour type give a percentage resistance to corresponding status effects, rather than prevent them alltogether. This would still provide benefits for having the armour, but it would allow a chance for status effects to happen, increasing the usefulness of a lot of skills early in the battles.
Other than that, most of my issues are simple things that are undoubtedly going to get fixed through testing: permanent blindness issues that carry over into new battles, lack of companion options outside of original 4 (meaning no tank option without building into it), a beginning where I felt like I was running around talking to people for hours with no real direction and no winnable battles.
All in all, this seems like a great improvement on an already amazing game. I can't wait for the final product.

So, this was a game that struck me a while back as a title deserving at least a look. I finally got around to it recently, and I'm regretfully sorry to say that I'm sorely disappointed in what I got. I play games like Software, Inc. & Mad Games Tycoon on a weekly basis. I'm a huge fan of economics strategy/simulator games, and take pride in my skill in them.
Don't get me wrong, I was drawn into this game like many others due to the stylistic nature and interesting subject choice. I like the cohesive aesthetic, the stylistic choices, and the general loose feel of the game. I indeed like the video editing activity, upgrading my setup, and even talking with people. Even if the video editing itself feels somewhat flawed, I still like it.
I would like to see the video editing take a less RNG-method of approach. It's very frustrating to sit down with an economy simulation title and be given a scenario with variables I can't control. The deck of cards is an interesting way to give character to my videos, but it's also an interesting way to unnecessarily frustrate the player. It feels like a rock, paper, scissors game when I only have two options at a time. Furthermore, the editing process itself feels almost flawed. Lining up arrows is a good way to identify smooth or rough transitions in a final video, but it feels like I'm constantly harassed by them, as well. I need some way to quickly identify how my arrows are going to turn out without being thrown to the wolves about it.
Secondly, I'm actually rather upset how the NPCs in this game treat the protagonist. The roommate comes in and commandeers my computer, my primary method of making money, and I get no say? People barge in my house and demand I go somewhere with them immediately or they won't like me as much? I get blasted for wanting some semblance of privacy? People constantly bombard the player with absolutely ridiculous requests, and often the player can't do anything about them. It's absolutely infuriating to finally get time to make a video, when suddenly the screen fills with an insane amount of absolute garbage people want done first. I don't have time for their problems, when their problems feel like the focus of the game.
On the topic of time, the game moves incredibly too fast. It honestly feels like the game is forcing me to constantly use up all my time as part of the mechanic. I buy a game one day, and can't actually make a video on it for 8 days. This is because either my computer has been comandeered, people who should be 'my friends' think I'm the only friend in the world they have, or I just spent 48 hours editting because I dared to stop and think about how to order the pieces. Then, I get a call on my phone and lose subscribers because I just want to be left alone, and the internet thinks I'm a heartless monster because of it. Then at last, when it's time to get a new game, the most recent one is a week old and I have no possible way of knowing (what is the internet again?) what games are coming out.
Finally, what truly gets my goat about this game is that it almost feels like there is no playstyle freedom or replay value available here. The consoles are the first problem; when all I own is a PC and all I want to own is a PC, that should be just as viable as owning everything. I constantly get invitations to upcoming games on other platforms that I've never played on. That makes no sense to begin with. On top of the consoles, though, is the 'story' of the game. It makes the whole game feel like it's on rails and I don't get the choice of doing anything how I like. I'm forced to have all the consoles, I'm forced to go to all the events, and worst of all: I'm forced to have collaborators and roommates. I understand the use of roommates, but it should be a choice. I understand the value of collaborators, but it should (again) be a choice. I understand the value of having all of the consoles, but it should be (one more time) a choice. In fact, the game is so badly railed up that I found it actually difficult to make a poor choice other than getting banned.
I can't say that my opinion won't change, which is why I'm not refunding the game at this point. However, I won't be recommending this game to anyone unless some of these poorly designed mechanics change. I truly do think this game has potential, but it's far from realized.

In Bioshock 2, former city council member Dr Sophia Lamb takes over Rapture 10 years after Bioshock 1, and continues the experiments on Big Daddies/Little Sisters.

The context is pretty original, it's based on theories that all social pathology is traced back to the single ego of each individual member of society. She argues that capitalism is the culmination of social individualism, because the economy generates value based in a notion of exclusivity, rooted in ego. Rapture under Ryan being the culmination of capitalism, would be the culmination of egocentric society.

She argues that capitalism glorifies individual ego mirrored in a notion of success propagated by the American Dream, and that the pursuit of happiness is just a front to justify our own desires. To free humanity from poverty, suffering and inequality, one has to let go of their own ego completely.

Rapture itself turns into a social experiment to refine this theory, to reshape humanity into this vision of "Utopia". You as the failed product of a bigone age, is the only one standing against her.

I loved playing L.A. Noire. The homicide desk is my favorite. It stays true to old-school noir-style storytelling while using advanced technology that places real actors' faces and facial expressions in the game. The story is compelling (this is a narrative game as opposed to a choices matter game; even though I prefer the latter, I did not mind that this game was the former- I think it worked better this way), the character designs are out of this world thanks to the motion camera technology, and the world is accurate to 1940s Los Angeles and beautiful (albeit for show and not really filled with content outside of the cases and collectibles). I was really immersed into the detective work and the lie detection system (which is the main gameplay, although there is also car chases, shootouts, brawling, and more!).
It took me thirty and a half hours to complete the main game (including DLC), but another almost fifteen hours to get 100% completion. My only wish is that Rockstar would follow their original plans of making the "Noir" games a series of games. I would buy LA/NY/Chicago/etc Noire 2 in a heartbeat even if it did not feature the original characters (who I also enjoyed getting to know/ controlling).

So, when I first saw Warshift release on Steam, I'll admit, I was pretty interested in playing it. I've always been a fan of those games that mix the genres to make something all new and interesting.
Warshift is a game that sells itself as an "experimental project where Action, RTS and RPG gameplay elements are combined in one space epic." Unfortunately, I don't think it does any of these well.
I bought this game wanting to like it, but I can't recommend playing it at any price point.
Lets start with the action. The controls are straightforward enough, but it can't quite figure out whether you're "Avatar" is supposed to be amazing or the same as the rest. When you go into battle, your character doesn't even always face the place your aiming, so with melee weaponry, it's hard to get a feel as to whether your even actually hitting the thing you're trying to. And when you get tired of being all upfront and personal, there's no indication of how far things are away, or if the shot you fired connects or hits that tree's leaves halfway there.
Of course, should you think this can be played purely as a RTS, you're mistaken there too. The moment you swap back from Action mode to Strategy mode the game immediately gives your unit new orders sending it off to fight the enemy. Sounds great right? Ha. No. If your Avatar dies, it rips you from strategy mode after a short 10 second-or-so countdown and send you to the customize-your-avatar screen.
Oh, speaking of your avatar, as you shoot things or attack things or kill things, you'll get levels of some sort. Honestly, these seem bolted on, and I don't have any idea what they actually do. Maybe that's from not playing enough, or not looking at the screen at the right time, but maybe this game would be a bit better if they stripped out the attempts at being a RPG, and stuck to trying to be an Action/RTS. Not that I think that would make it something I'd want to play.

TL;DR
For being a free, this game is completely worth what you get. You have agility beyond belief which allows for more than a 'CoD like shooter', and extensive modding which doesn't "dumb down" the player at all. Quite literally billions of mod combinations! This game has a fluidity which doesn't allow for a review to do it justice. What does that mean? Well, the nearly monthly, FREE updates, can completely change this game. With the Plains of Eidolon just on the horizon, this game will go from mission based to open world. This is the sort of game that gets updates which seem like Warframe 2. Imagine Destiny, but Destiny 2 was a free update. It's a great game, honestly. Not P2W at all, and is SO generous you'll probably spend money just to donate to DE! I highly recommend this game. Why not try it? It's free!
Intro
Warframe, a universe thriving with lush, hidden lore. The place where a species of technologically crude, and industrious Grineer have made home. The place where a plutocratic, advanced, and money greedy Corpus have made home. The place where a technocyte plague known as the Infestation has made home. Ah, and of course.. the place where you, the noble, honorable, Tenno; have made home.
Warframe Pros
Warframe is a free to play done right, everything in this game can be earned for completely free. You know how I know? Well, I've been getting EVERYTHING for free, and have spent a fair amount of hours to get this info!
This game has thousands of mods. Unlike its 'comparable' Destiny, this game has more than a dumbed down skill tree. This game has a modding system. One which lets your power have billions of stat combos.
This game allows for player to player trading. Whether you're looking for 'prime' gear, or platinum (premium currency), trading has you covered. There are people willing to trade you for mods, gear, and platinum.
The UPDATES, now this is a big one. This game Warframe has had so many updates, nearly on a monthly basis that it could EASILY have had a Warframe 2 by now. For a game being completely free, these updates are WELL worth your time. I mean hell, for the first time, we're getting an enormous expansion adding open worlds! (which we all know will be expanded to every planet).
The memorable moments. One, undeniable fact, is that this game gets sweeter as time goes on. With monumental quests such as The Second Dream and The War Within, this game will blow you out of your socks. Though, for some, this can take up to 100-200 hours to get to. It's crazy, but gives you the best feeling and memory afterwards.
Your Space Mom. Every Tenno needs to feel like they have someone.. SOMEONE! For the longest time, in the game, I was closest to my dear space mom. The Lotus!
The soundtrack is absolutely gorgeous, I know this is a random one but it can really hit you in the feels later on. Try looking up "This is What You Are - Keith" <- It'll bring you to a Warframe song that is too good..
Warframe Cons
The grind can be unrelenting for some. For people like me, the grind was never bad because of my constant progression, but for people who aren't patient or want things quickly (in a progression system) this might be a bit too much.
The lore is very hidden. There is a story, but for some major lore, and theories on it, you'll have to look it up on YouTube. If you'd like a good series I recommend StallorD
The enemy scaling. For some people who love a hard challenge, the enemy scaling might be too much. Not exactly the ENEMY itself, but more specifically the ARMOUR on an enemy. It can be insane to even damage an enemy after level 100.
Improvements?
These are simply opinions on minor things...
Dojo improvements. I think Tennogen should be introduced for the Dojo, more decorations should be added, AND massive group builds. I'm talking about decorations that require a load of resources. That way if you have a large and active clan, you'll have special things that show your true power, and riches!
On 'Finisher' animations for the Nikana backslash, a mark/bodysplit hould happen. What I mean is that you do a diagonal slash across the enemies back, yet no deep cut appears, or body splitting? I dunno, just a request!
Final Words
Now please, note that this is all speculation and pure opinions! I love Warframe! If you have any questions, need help in game, a clan to join, or notice anything spelled wrong, or anything I should add.. please feel free to drop a comment in the space below!

I generally don't write reviews.  That said, this game will be one of the exceptions to that, since it richly deserves one.  My first play ended badly at times, getting stun-locked sucks whatever game you are playing.  But, as I reloaded, I learned.  Physical/Magical armor to counter conditions, use the terrain, which I've never really thought about in games, as it generally  doesn't do anything, even use your opponent's skills against them.  Stunlock the raging enemies, since they are easier to hit. Use teleport to move enemies to where they are less able to give you headaches.  So much fun to watch them run over the same path several times and just get teleported back to where they were.  Guerilla tactics where necessary.  Consider to whom you speak when making attempts at persuasion/intimidation.  It's really nice to have a tactics game where the computer is really good at making strategic decisions.  I would give it an 8.5 out of 10.  Excellent grasp of party tactics, good number of alternate paths to accomplish goals, skills system is easy to understand once you study it a bit, combat is intuitive, and combos are easy to make and can cause serious mayhem.  On the other hand, the story is short, and there are bugs, the blind condition can sometimes take a save and reload to clear, clothing will clip oddly at times, and unlike the description, you can't as yet play the undead.
