The most misunderstood game of the past 10 years judging by the forum, reddit and other forums. No, just because it got published under the Rockstar brand, doesn't mean it's another GTA, yet people ask it all the time, "is it like GTA?", "I thought it was like GTA", "Why isn't it like GTA" <- which would be like asking why Manhunt or Midnight Club aren't GTA.
After playing through this game a couple times and replaying it currently i thought i write a review, can't hurt and to make it short: No, it's not GTA if anything it's like the old Police Quest games from Sierra, not as strict in the "Be a police man" style but the overall tone is quite the same.
You're some sort of troubled war veteran, Cole Phelps who joins the LAPD. The game is quite linear in that you follow a story, Phelps' story from being a street cop to getting into the bigger departments like Vice and Homicide with bigger cases, you can't really control his outcome but you can control the cases.
You start as a lowly street cop tracking down some burglaries and violence, getting promoted soon to investigate murder,  blackmailing, drug and alcohol bootlegging as well as arson. The game as i said plays out like Police Quest, more like an advenure. You go to a crime scene, you investigate the crime scene look for clues and then you go to interrogate witneseses and suspectes.
This is where teh game really shines, the facial animations along with the voice ovrs are still the best you can find in games even today, they are highly realistic and that's what the game needs since it wants you to telll if somebody is lying, hiding something or telling the truth, watch them while they talk and get to your own concolussion.
And it only works if you do your detective job, collect items, look up stuff, even a matchbook can be a important clue and you better have a sharp eye.
The game takes place in 1947 Los Angeles and the cases all are either recreations or being inspired by real life cases, the city is recreated, there are original songs on the radio and the entire game really feels like the USA just shortly after the war.
The only negative point are the graphics, weird shadows, pixellations and in some (not mine but there are enough reports) frame drops are a frequent problem, it's not a good port but it's playable and there are no crashes (i played through  the game on several computers over the years, running from windows xp to windows 7 even)
Playing it again nowadays again, i can only say that i really enjoy the game, it's awesome and a lot of fun. It gets better once you realize that most of the stuff happened in real life as the 1947projet on blogspot shows, it has the original cases and inspirations for the game, it's really amazing.

I received the default warframe but with a few golden stripes(exclusive only to the founders omg worth it -.-), default pistol with a few more golden stripes, and the default melee weapon with even more golden stripes. All in all i paid for golden stripes. So where is the p2w factor? Everything, everywhere. In the game you can build items in your foundry with resources that you gathered in missions, which is essentially your only way of getting new weapons. And when you build things it takes time, as mentioned above 12/24 hours for most weapons and 72 hours for warframes. or you can just pay. yep, just pay some money and you can instantly skip the waiting time and get much much more time to progress than average f2p players. Oh whats that? Lazy to collect resources to build? Worry not! Just pay more money! Yes thats right, buy resources. Wait what? too lazy to even build? Fear not! Just BUY THE ACTUAL WEAPON AND WARFRAME FROM THE MARKET. Oh and there is a trading system, that yes, the paid in game currency, platinum, is the only currency that can be traded. So you say your desired prime weapon or prime warframe is not inside the market? Fear not just buy if off other players!  Although warframe isn't meant to be a competitive game, but the shear fact that you can spend hundreds of hours on a weapon/warframe that someone else can just obtain it by buying it within seconds, is kind of discouraging the farming aspect.
Either you play with friends, or get ready to solo your entire journey in warframe. Its near impossible to find friends because of how complicated the friend system is. You have to go through 4 screens to add a friend. Press esc, bring up a whole list of buttons, click community which shows how lonely you are with no friends, then click add friend which show another big black box with a search bar that does not auto-fill in existing player names or even let you know if the name you typed even exists, and after you click on add there is another pop-up asking if you are sure you want friends. Clan system? Clan exclusive unlockables exists in this game, weapons mainly, and you contribute your hard earned resources to this makeshift dojo that nobody outside the clan can visit or in fact nobody visits, and the p2w players just buy resources and skip research time to instantly obtain these unlockable weapons. Which of course the f2p clans will takes weeks if not months, if they have with inactive players, to unlock. Oh and also, as a "legendary" founder, there is a founder "exclusive" design chat that supposely founders can share they enthusiasm for the game and share new warframe or weapon ideas and designs or even new content. Nah who am i joking. Been playing this game for 3 years and the chat is dead, nobody says anything at all. Except for the occasional "Is this chat fully dead yet" questions popping up.

Simply put. This game is fun. And that's what a game should be. It's like what happens when you mix old school platforming with a beatem up arcade game and throw in MMORPG elements. For me that's almost a dream come true. the combat is action based and while you CAN get away with spamming your basic attacks through the game. You get more enjoyment if you look into how your character'c combos work and link together.
Some negatives:
~The inventory space is limited unless you pay for more space. It's not unbearable but it can be semi-frustrating.
~The b-slot on your skill slots is locked unless you pay for it. Some people view it as essential and I can see that being the case for some characters but not all. I'm using Ara Haan and havent found any problems with just the a-slot but when I play as Chung I do tend to want more skills available.
~MOST cosmetic changes are only availble through real cash. Especially the cool ones. Other Cosmetic changes are gained through rare drops.
~The player shops are pricy. Very pricy. But once again you don't HAVE to go in there.
~It's grindy... were you expecting that to change from other MMOs?
~No super awesome CGI scenes. Sorry guys. Trailers are the best it gets.
~The Steam launcher runs through Internet Explorer -.-
Now the Positives:
~FUN. Just straight up fun. My gf and I downloaded this game at the same time. We are both on our second characters (we kind of abandoned our firsts after level 40) and are both level 50. For me that's a true testament to this game because with most MMOs I don't play past level 25.
~All real money purchases are COMPLETELY OPTIONAL! This game is truly play for free. It is not a pay to win formula! (though if you really want a mount that's gonna run you about 20 bucks but it's not neccessary).
~It's a low intensity game on your computer. Meaning if you have a bottom of the line computer you can probably play it. Though I reccomend at least a bottom of the line graphics card. This translates to running almost flawlessly in midrange gaming computers on maximum settings.
~Though the graphics are cute, they aren't too cute. Raven, Elsword and the Dealdy Chaser/Tactical Trooper Chung still look ****ing awesome.
~All cutscenes/talking scenes are skippable. And though the game is not story driven and can be played without the slightest Idea as to how all the characters relate it is still interesting for those that want to take the time for the cutscenes.
~PVP is a little laggy but fun. Be warned it is spam happy and works radically different from the PVE. This is a great place to learn how characters actually combo. PvE is easy in comparison
Here's the point, I have gotten over at least 100+ hours of enjoyment out of this game. The only game on my account that comes close to that is Sonic Generations (which i payed for) and that's because I modded the living hell out of it. So knowing that this game was free and that it has provided me with this much gameplay and knowing that there is STILL two more in game regions to play through. I don't mind throwing a little bit of cash at it. Some people may find this game repetitive and boring and then go back to their good 'ol Call of Duty. Good for them. I'm gonna keep playin and I think you should give it a shot too.

I should have written a review long ago.  After all, I've played this game for 1,000+ hours and idle'd in its level editor for a few hundred more.
Dustforce DX is the deepest and most technically demanding 2D platformer ever made.  It has a momentum based engine where all actions have real weight and consequence, attacks have start-up frames, things are jump and dash-cancellable, and there are tricks measured in how many frames they save.  Every level has leaderboards both for score and for raw time, and the community is fiercly competitive and still very active.  More importantly, every run on the leaderboards also has a replay embedded.  Being able to watch your run (or anyone else's) is not just fun, it's a fantastic learning tool.  If that sounds like something you'd enjoy, then keep reading.
Dustforce DX will never hold the player's hand.  Several people ragequit the third TUTORIAL, and a wide number of the advanced mechanics and workings of the game are never explained in-game.  To really master this game and understand everything in it, you need to know other people who play it and/or engage on the subreddit and IRC channel.  Even if you do that and arm yourself with knowledge: this game is HARD.  When you think you've finally gotten good and beaten the game, you have only just begun because you unlocked "The Difficults".  Honestly even getting that far is going to take you a hundred hours at least, because the only way to unlock new levels is to complete easier levels perfectly.  I'll explain...
Dustforce DX has 4 main hub areas of one large world (The Nexus).  Each hub has 4 baby levels, 4 easy levels, 4 medium levels, and 4 exceedingly hard levels.  Each tier of level above the first is locked by a key, and you earn progress toward keys by playing the levels in the tier below.  But the only way to get a full key from 1 single level is to get an SS rank.  One S is completion: for cleaning all the dust and defeating all the enemies.  The other S is Finesse: for never losing your combo from dying, getting hit, or letting it time out.  The game doesn't just reward perfection, it demands it if you even want to see all the stock levels.
Now why did I say stock levels you may ask?  That's because the true magic of this game is its INTENSELY POWERFUL level editor.  Custom Dustforce Maps (it calls them maps instead of levels) are what keep me playing.  This is one of several games where the editor gives you every tool the dev had, letting you make stuff on par with, and often exceeding, the quality of the stock game.  You have 20 layers to work with, tons of cool props, almost complete RGB color control and control over the %blend of the color PER LAYER, a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of props and emitters to place, several things with transparency for awesome effects, and total control over the music and sound effects at every point.  The last sentence is very important since this game has a truly amazing soundtrack.  Free control over the music in the editor doubles as a sound test, even if you don't enjoy making maps.  The nice thing about the leaderboards and replays is that you can watch everyone playing your map once you publish it.  That adds another level of enjoyment to the process, a feature missing from several other games with level editors.
There are almost no restrictions on what you can place anywhere, allowing the free mixing of themes from the 4 hubs if you have the skill to make it work.  The game is easily moddable and the community has several killer spritemods available, one even turns a character into Kirby!  There are several different classes of mods both for art and for performance, and they are all easy enough to find on the subreddit.  Sadly they aren't integrated into Steam like with many other games.  The community also has several third party tools available for more detailed stat-tracking, new kinds of competition, and even a cool TAS community.
In conclusion, Dustforce DX is a great game and one of my all time favorites.  It's not easy to get into: indeed you will struggle if you go it alone and it's still very difficult even with friends beside you.  You'll get what you put into it.  We still learn things about this game every week; the engine is just that deep.  A lot of the quirks in this game are things you just won't find anywhere else.  When I say that there's no 2D platformer with the complexity of Dustforce... I mean it.

Dustforce is a really smooth platform game, with a big focus on stylish and fast ways to clear the levels. With an included level editor, and leaderboards available for all levels ever uploaded- it becomes a very competetive experience, especially since you can watch every (!) player's replay in-game.
You can try to redo their runs and improve upon them- to climb the leaderboards, and feel like the king of the big internet arcade.
The game itself is very challenging, but selfexplanatory and easy to learn. The progress you make as a player is always clearly visible and definitely satisfying. If you want online challenges- there's plenty available; if you want to play just for yourself- there are medals at the end of each level, to reward you with a bit of singleplayer experience.
It's big, fun, and sometimes frustrating to play; but even if you can't get very far- there is always the great artstyle to gaze upon, and chill soundtrack to soothe your nerves (not to mention level editor, where you can make your own kind of experience).
I love this game and I definitely recommend it; but it's hard for me to tell whether I like the game better, or just it's beautiful soundtrack (STRONGLY ADVISED TO PLAY THE TRAILER).

I generally don't write reviews.  That said, this game will be one of the exceptions to that, since it richly deserves one.  My first play ended badly at times, getting stun-locked sucks whatever game you are playing.  But, as I reloaded, I learned.  Physical/Magical armor to counter conditions, use the terrain, which I've never really thought about in games, as it generally  doesn't do anything, even use your opponent's skills against them.  Stunlock the raging enemies, since they are easier to hit. Use teleport to move enemies to where they are less able to give you headaches.  So much fun to watch them run over the same path several times and just get teleported back to where they were.  Guerilla tactics where necessary.  Consider to whom you speak when making attempts at persuasion/intimidation.  It's really nice to have a tactics game where the computer is really good at making strategic decisions.  I would give it an 8.5 out of 10.  Excellent grasp of party tactics, good number of alternate paths to accomplish goals, skills system is easy to understand once you study it a bit, combat is intuitive, and combos are easy to make and can cause serious mayhem.  On the other hand, the story is short, and there are bugs, the blind condition can sometimes take a save and reload to clear, clothing will clip oddly at times, and unlike the description, you can't as yet play the undead.

Contrast was a compelling, whimsical journey. The storyline was interesting, the game mechainics fun and challenging and above all else the art took my breath away. I feel like talking about constrast I don't want to review a game but a story. Usually I'd play a game and ignore the cut scenes, the background, the story. I'd smash through the levels in periodic runs and then come back months later and finish it off. Contrast defies this. Even if you're struggling with the gameplay the beauty of the colour world tempts you to stay in the game and keep throwing yourself between worlds in the hope you'll stumble over the way forward. The music is haunting and a perfect compainion to the detailed artwork and graphics. The mechanics are as flawless and artistic as the rest of the game.
In the game you play as "Dawn", the imaginary friend of a little girl in search of her father, or an adventure, it really doesn't seem to matter. Dawn is the only character visible in the 3D colour world, what seems like the real world to the player, while all other characters are seen only as shadows. We assume that the real world is in fact the grim shadow plane after some story progression. It's this concept that creates the game's coolest and most novel mechanic; Dawn's ability to shift into a shadow and interect with the other shadows as if playing a 2D game. This description might sound wordy and confusing, but trust me, you won't be able to resist playing with it and with just a click you can hop between the game's dimensions.
Overall it's quite easy to play. Me, a novice, managed well and found it just the right difficulty to challange but also be overcomeable without the help of walkthroughs. More skilled players might find the game easy to beat however the real point of Contrast is the storyline that encourages you to play and explore the world, find objects that provide more clues to the story and figure it out at your own pace. I don't need to say anything about the game itself when I say it's worth playing just for the sensory delight.

I'm honestly uncertain if most of the negative reviews are legitimate or just getting on the meme train of space to crash.
I waited months to actually play this game due to all the negative crash reviews. I waited until patches. Then saw more negative crash reviews. The last patch came out. More negative reviews. After 4 more months, I finally said screw it and took my chances. I went into this with what is known now (despite being a game approach that has existed forever) as the Bethesda Method. Save often and obsessively because it will crash.
I started the game. No issues. I kept playing. No crashes. I then decided to read more to see where the crash issues were. The space issue was never a problem for me. I found that people were having the crash issue after lengthy playing sessions. I never did. The other problem point was around Futuristics. I got to that point... no crashes.
Full disclosure: The game crashed for me twice. Due to auto saving and my own saving, this didn't cause me any game loss. One of those points was when I was protecting a little sister when she was harvesting. I forget the level but it was in front of a stage in a room with a balcony. Lots of enemies, lots of explosions. The second time was an ambush  when I was leaving an office later in the game. Again, enemies, explosions. None of  these are anything I put as unforeseen with a game like this that was for console and older.
Now, will this be case for everyone? No clue. My personal experience was just fine. If you are like me and played the original Bioshock and Infinite and want to play this game that you missed when it was released, take the plunge. Save often just in case. And who knows, the playthrough might be clear enough to make you feel silly that you saved so obsessively to begin with. Gameplay wise, Bioshock 2 is the most enjoyable out of the trilogy.

Bioshock 2 is the sequel to the acclaimed first person shooter Bioshock, still set in the underwater city of Rapture 8 years after the first game. The player takes control of one of the first Big Daddies, on a quest to rescue his grown-up Little Sister. Unlike the first Bioshock, this game was developed by 2K Marin. The remastered edition includes all the DLCs.
+While not as memorable as Bioshock's storyline, this sequel's plot is still a solid, emotional and deep journey through the fallen utopia of Rapture in search of the one thing we care about in this crapsack world. It's good enough to keep you interested, and has some good twists while greatly expanding the city's lore and backstory with the usual ton of audio diaries scattered around the environments.
+The gunplay and fighting system is a welcomed improvement, thanks to being able to use a firearm in the right hand and a plasmid in the left without having to constantly switch during combat. This system makes combos much easier and satisfying to pull off without making them bland, and as a result fighting is much more enjoyable.
+The setting and level design is as great as ever. While, for obvious reasons, Rapture isn't as astonishing as it used to be the first time around, you'll still be visiting the beautifully rotting locations and creepy yet fascinating halls this city's made of. Levels are also large, filled with stuff to collect and very detailed, so they're a pleasure to explore.
+Audio, from the soundtrack to voice acting, is very good. I would only question the sound effects, that sometimes are weirdly muffled.
+The Minerva's Den DLC is a worthy experience, albeit being completely separated from the main campaign. It's a bit short perhaps, but it's a good story and it's a good addition to the base package.
+Fighting Big Daddies is as cool as ever, even though being a Big Daddy yourself you'd expect a more evenly matched fight. Instead you are either at a massive disadvantage or massively overpowered. Fighting Big Sisters is however always thrilling and adequately hard.
-This "remastered" edition, unlike the one Bioshock 1 was given, has no graphical makeover at all, rather simply including all the available DLC...
-...which, excluding Minerva's Den, isn't even particularly amazing, being lame arenas to slay waves of enemies in and not much else.
-A multiplayer mode is oddly available for this game (it was the excruciating time when games just HAD to have some online PvP gamemode, even when it was horrendously forced to), but, while it isn't atrocious per se, it's nothing memorable either, and it's mostly deserted at this point in time.
-Protecting Little Sisters while they harvest Adam is coherent with you being a Big Daddy, and it's a good change to play defensively from time to time, but it's also really time-consuming, and it can get repetitive.
-Not being able to backtrack is a very poor design decision, even if it's justified plot-wise. When you leave an area you leave it for good, which forces the enterprising player to spend a lot of time in each area instead of clearing them and returning later to wipe them clean of loot. Some won't mind, myself included, but others certainly will.
-Graphics aren't terrible and they are surely improved over the first game's, but it's safe to say that the Unreal Engine 2.5 or something used in this game doesn't really age too well.
Being a "more of the same" sequel who wasn't even produced by the original developers (Irrational Games), Bioshock 2 is often dismissed as a cash grab sequel that most diehard fans of the series (along with the third installment itself, Bioshock Infinite) refuse to acknowledge. In my humble opinion, Bioshock 2, while nothing too spectacular, is still a solid game with a good plot, cool and unique mechanics and a beautiful atmosphere and setting that deserves to be played. As I've adored Bioshock 1 and only wished for more time to spend in Rapture, this game was exactly what I needed. If you, too, feel like that, then buying this game is a good idea. If you already own the base game, fear not: you'll be automatically given a copy of this edition.

As a remake of the classic NES title "Bionic Commando", this game got the full HD treatment - widescreen support, a kick@ss soundtrack by Payday composer Simon Viklund, a complete graphical overhaul with 3D characters, co-op mode, and more.
The negative reviews for this seem to be about the control scheme - which stays true to its classic NES roots. There is NO jumping in this game - every vertical move you make is using your bionic arm. Hence the title, BIONIC COMMANDO. Figuring out what paths to take to get where you want to go is part of the fun. If you can't (or refuse to) figure it out for yourself, you shouldn't be playing this game.

Intel Core i7 950 @ 3.06GHz
8GB Team Elite RAM
GigaByte Nvidia GeForce GTX 460 1GB (Slightly overclocked)

When I entered the world of DOS 2 for the first time, I was instantly blown away by the graphics.  The new world is simply stunning, the artwork amazing and that alone made me instantly appreciate the game.  As I played a couple of the characters, I recognized that each of them have some sort of flaw, past, something unknown driving them and a big part of the game is me figuring what that is and it is going to lead to a great story. That one thing alone is a huge timesaver after a battle as in DOS it would take me time to apply all of the various heals to get my characters up again if there were no beds about.  I do hope they will come up with something for repairs so that in game I don't have to spend so much time repairing every single slot on the character page.
So do I recommend this game? Hell, yes.  However, it is alpha so think of it as a preview of what I think could become the game of the year for 2017. (No pressure Devs)  It will be some time before you can get to the end game on this one.  If that will frustrate you, I would say wait.  BUT, if you want to alpha test and watch a game develop as you play you HAVE to go ahead and buy this one, you are going to want to when it is fully released anyway.

Cons:
-Game requires you to buy extra slots if you want to have a wide veriaty of inventory space, skills during dungeons, quick use items, and storage space (bank).
-The game is based around a sort of time limit of play per character wich is measured by the stamana bar at the bottom right of the screen. Granted if you play dungeons with other players, the bar decreases at a much slower rate. Once depleted you cannot access dungeons, but you can still go around in the hub world and grind at the fields against generic enemies and the occasional field boss that appears about every 10-20 min if people in the feild are defeating the generic enemies.
-Outfits....you can forget about full custimization freedom, most of the awesome stuff is in the store (as in IRL cash). Lvling up after lvl 34 starts to drag so be ready to take on side quests or grind at the fields.
-Lastly, you will be given a quest to change job class when you reach the appropiate lvl. this isnt usually a problem, but the tick is that when you take on the second job class you will be asked to obtain a certain amount of an item that, from what ive seen, has a drop rate of about 5-8%. Depending on the character and job class path taken, you will be asked to find an item in the varrying amounts of 10-100 (research your character if you have the time and want to put in the effort for them).
Pros:
-Anime style 2d beatem up that can provide hours of enjoyment. Sure the cons may look bad, but ive had this game for two years and recently linked it with steam.
-While you dont have full customization freedom, you have the oppertunity to find armor that looks different and cooler compared to the generic drops. They are harder to get, but get the full set and you will look cool AND get stat bonuses.
-Events are frequent and sometimes give you the option of obtaining and keeping an item that will be available only within that time period. first you obtain a temperary version then engage event quests to make the item permanent. Keep an eye on the news page as this will alert you to anything of the sort and go for it as soon as you see an event like so. Usually if an event goes on and offers an outfit or costume of some type with the added oppertunity to make it permanent, it will require you to complete and event quest nearly the entire month/week/etc in order to obtain the sufficiant quest rewards to do so, but in the end its worth it, because you didnt pay a thing.
-while it costs IRL money to obtain expansion to your inventory and of the like, you will not need it. What you have is enough unless you are a horder, in which case you may need some help.
-P2W (Pay-to-Win)? Nope. While you can buy items in the shop, you can obtain gear just as equal or better through your hard work. Accessory drops are also available in most dungeons (at an unbeliveable drop rate for some) that will give you stats boosts and give your character some added cosmetic look.

world, only then, can the Christian, theist, moralist and agnostic piece together the true wonders of the universe and of the ultimate reality of a dystopian underworld, hence, Rapture.
The main character in the game, and whom we end up playing as is named Johnny Topside. He is only referred to as Big Daddy and through one of the antagonists, Grace Holloway, ‘ Tin Daddy.’  We see our main foils, Andrew Ryan, the mastermind behind Rapture’s founding and creation has a much different vision than that of Dr. Sofia Lamb. Andrew Ryan is loosely based on the legacy of Ayn Rand, who was an existentialist philosopher, but by the time her two most noteworthy works came out, existentialism was already a philosophy grounded on social progress and severe individualism, which gave rise to socialism later on in postmodernism and the rise of the bourgeoisie and proletariat classes. A detective game drawing major influences from the old film noir movies (e.g. The Naked City) and other crime dramas (think Chinatown (1974) and The Untouchables (1987)).
It has one of the most polished stories I've ever seen in video games with a lot of the cases being references to era-specific murder cases such as the Black Dahlia mystery. The protagonist (Detective Cole Phelps) is an amazingly well fleshed-out character who goes through a major transformation as the story unfolds. A gritty portrayal of the life of a detective in the 1940s accentuated by the remarkable dialogue.
The investigation part of L.A. Noire is divided into two parts. First you inspect the crime scene for any clues pertaining to the case (Trust me you'll hear a lot of "Hmm, takes a smarter man than me to figure this one out.")

After that you will start interviewing and or interrogating witnesses and or suspects. Now this is the part of the game where you make the case harder or easier on yourself. Based on the clues you've gathered from a crime scene and other interrogations you can ask questions. Which, after answered, the player can respond to with either Truth, Lie or Doubt. You must figure out which one to choose based on previous clues and facial expressions.
When you guess wrong this may lead to you having to start over or worse missing a clue which can make solving the crime a whole lot harder.
The gunplay in this game isn't really that remarkable and that isn't necessarily a bad thing because, seeing as you are still a cop, the main goal is obviously to take most of the suspects into custody. If you are looking for a game set in the same era with lots of gunplay you are better off with Mafia II.
Driving around in this game is another great part of it, you can listen to the dialogue between Cole and his partner about the case, whatever's going on in their life and finally the radio. L.A. Noire has an amazing soundtrack filled with era appropriate songs by Ella Fitzgerald, Bing Crosby, Charlie Parker, etc.
You can also respond to thefts in progress which are basically the side missions in L.A. Noire. As for the city of Los Angeles and its authenticity:
Although the city is so beautiful and life-like there really isn't that much to do in the free roam part of the game. I feel like that's Rockstar's missed opportunity in this game, they brought this amazing city to life but they didn't do anything with it. I would've appreciated some restaurants or bars to sit down with Cole and his partner outside of the storyline.
L.A. Noire is one of my all-time favorite games with amazing gameplay, a superb story that unfolds against the backdrop of Los Angeles in the forties and a great character arc. If you find yourself intrigued by crime dramas and want to crawl into the skin of a detective this is the game for you. You have to understand that this isn't a "run around and kill people" type of game which is Rockstar’s specialty. With a playtime of about 30 hours (and that's only cases, I never free roam) it's well worth its money and you'll very quickly get invested in this masterpiece.
It is an amazing homage to the film noir genre and detective stories. So, grab yourself a couple of cold brewskis and get swept away.

LA Noire is an great game in many respects, but it is entirely impossible to recommend the title on the PC. Put simply, this may be the worst console port I have ever had the displeasure of enduring.
Firstly, the game is capped at 30fps due to the engine's physics being tied the game's framerate. I wouldn't consider this a dealbreaker in and of itself, but at this framerate the game suffers extremely noticeable microstutter which makes it nearly unplayable for me. There exists a workaround to run the game at 60fps, but, as expected, this causes the game to freak out. The result is cars with hilariously terrible handling and inflated acceleration. I have also seen it reported that it may cause some characters' facial animations to become desynced, although I have not observed this issue myself in my limited playtime.
Secondly, I have consistently suffered from a bug where alt-tabbing to minimize the fullscreen game window and then returning to the game will cause the display refresh rate to change to 24Hz, furthering excacerbating the stuttering problem. This bug can be fixed by using a command line in the launcher to force the game to run in windowed mode. Personally, I would much prefer a borderless windowed mode, but I didn't have the patience to investigate whether or not this was possible by this point. I was already becoming very frustrated at all the hoops I had to jump through to fix this game.
The final cherry on top is that, after all these years, the game still has integrated Rockstar Social Club DRM and it is required to sign in to a Social Club account to play the game. If the Social Club application ever fails you, you will be unable to proceed past the title screen.
Beyond the most pressing issues, I also noticed that the game has severe pop-in.
I'd give this one a pass.
Yes, it has a MASSIVE learning curve though, be very wary.

While I dislike that there is no real character progression save for a battle scar or two (thus enough time spent cannot make the dungeons easy ala rogue legacy or ftl) the sheer number of classes, items, and monsters keeps each run into the dungeons feeling fresh.
The writing is comedic and sarcastic, all to a tune, so its very reminiscent of the bards tale, which I heartily enjoy. The narrator has this not surprised tone of voice whenever he sings about your latest death, as though he has seen all this before.
The game is fairly simple, using random cards dealt to you, you build dungeons for your characters to run through, placing monsters in their path for them to defeat and grow stronger from, placing treasures, and building paths to specific objectives, but the cards you get are randomized every time. While you will see the same cards over and over again, the random nature keeps it from getting too stale, though it will get repetative.
The battle system is also the same, each class starts with a small deck of cards representing their skills, and you use them to fight monsters. As you don't fight with skill lists, but rather build attack decks as you go ala dominion, the game can at times come across as unfair, with you having to face off against bosses without the right abilities or equipment, or not being a high enough level. Summary: Some deaths are bullcrap and you will feel cheated, but it doesn;t happen often enough to be a problem.
The hand drawn asthetic is charming, like a board game someone drew up in a basement for their friends to play. If you are looking for a serious tone, you will not find it here.

Elsword is a side-scrolling arcade style beat-em-up, the game shines in the different classes and unlocking new ablities.  they recently made leveling ALOT easier and you can get your final job advancement (2nd one) in 3-4 days unless your playing on a saturday or sunday.  The reason i say this is because Elsword has a stamina system that goes down whenever you kill monsters in the fields, or when a monster dies in a dungeon.  Stamina is reset every night and all character's have seperate stamina bars, so if you run out of stamina on one character, just switch to another.  Also the maximum characters per account (without buying any) has increased from 3 to i believe 6.  A problem is that there is no character cuztomization if you dont spend real money, and the job advancement clothes they give you only last up to 2 weeks before getting deleted.  This makes some characters (like chung in my opinion) look really stupid, most others look fine though.  some events have given out costumes but these are rare.  The combat is nice and fluid as you can chain abilities with combos, and there are about 16 abilities per character but you can only have four of them on your skill bar, you can sawp them but they only give you enough SP (skill points) to max out around 6 so choose wisely (at each advancement you get a free potion that givs you back all your SP).  For i think 10 dollars you can unlock 4 extra abilit slots for one character,  but most abilities take 100 mana and your max is 300 so this is not essential to beat dungeons.  dungeons are easy early on but they get harder to beat later in the game, the way they do this is kind of wierd.  Good healing consumables have to be bought or can be crafted with materials you get in dungeons (either way works) but after level 40 it becomes a struggle to stay alive.  its works like this, there are around 30 to maybe 50 enimes per entire dungeon after level 40, my one character has around 100k hp but a single enemy hit can hit me 1k to possibly 10k depending on what it is so killing enemies efficiently and not getting hit is the name of the game.  life items can be found in boxes in the dungeons but these are used upon touching them are not abundent enough to sustain you through the entire game, on top of that the only way to get revives are though field bosses (rare to get revives from them), events, or buying them with real money.  its hard to explain but PvP's are decieded by whoever can chain more combos with abilities without knocking down the opponent (this sorta goes for PvE to but on a lesser scale), unless your in a 3v3 match and have team mates to interrupt the combo (start playing the game and it will make more sense).  i have friends who i play with so i dont interact with the community that much but guilds are the way to go to socialize as dungeons are usually too crazy with all the fighting to type to each other.  last thing i would like to point out is any dungeon can be entered from anywhere and you can que for 4 player parties or just start instantly with whoever is in your party.  all in all the game has its cons but being a free to play game it is worth a try as they are adding new content on a fairly regualr bases. now if youll exscuse me my fingers hurt.

Contrast is a wonderful little gem of a game, a clever original in a sea of sameness.  It's still rare to find adult games with a female protagonist, let alone one where she is tasked with looking after a young girl.  Thanks to a simple but highly effective story about family and redemption set against the backdrop of 1920s Paris and juxtaposed with a sci-fantasy theme, Contrast keeps you engaged thoughout.
The characters, dialogue, and voice acting are all first rate, and the jazzy noir soundtrack captures the mood perfectly.  The style and art direction (not to mention the sci-fi themes) reminded me a lot of Bioshock Infinite.  They struck a great balance between dark, whimsical, and surreal.  The principle game mechanic of shifting between 3D and the 2D world of shadows is done seamlessly.  The puzzles are clever and challenging but not frustrating, and feel very organic in the game's environments.  Moving about the game world, including the platform jumping elements, played very smoothly using my XBox controller.  The pacing between story and gameplay is spot on.  The story itself, about a girl, her nightclub singing mother, and transient stepfather, is tightly written and has a lot of heart.  And unlike a lot of games in recent years (Mass Effect 3, cough), they stick the landing with the ending, providing closure with just the right amount of explanation to keep you thinking long afterward about some of the themes the game touches on regarding the nature of our universe.
While Contrast is a short game, there is nothing wrong with being short when there are no wasted moments and both story and gameplay keep you interested every minute, just like a good book or movie.  A shame this game was not received very well when it came out, it's one of the most unique games I have played in a long time.

Great game. The first has become a favorite of mine and this one seems to be improving upon in in a lot of ways. However, there are a few things that I think could use some work. As this is an early access game, I truly hope that the Dev's are looking into these reviews. I have no idea how to give them constructive criticism outside of this forum. I guess I will try their website next.
My issues: The new armor system is an awesome addition. It changes battle strategy in amazing ways. However, it is truly unfortunate that no status effects can be given to anyone who still has even a sliver of corresponding armour. This ruins the early battle efficiency of a number of spells and abilities, and unless you spend time wittling each enemies armour down before killing them off (a terrible tactical plan) most AOE skills (namely spells) have very little value. My suggestion to fix this would be to have each point in an armour type give a percentage resistance to corresponding status effects, rather than prevent them alltogether. This would still provide benefits for having the armour, but it would allow a chance for status effects to happen, increasing the usefulness of a lot of skills early in the battles.
Other than that, most of my issues are simple things that are undoubtedly going to get fixed through testing: permanent blindness issues that carry over into new battles, lack of companion options outside of original 4 (meaning no tank option without building into it), a beginning where I felt like I was running around talking to people for hours with no real direction and no winnable battles.
All in all, this seems like a great improvement on an already amazing game. I can't wait for the final product.

If you haven't given Dustforce a shot by now, you should. The skill ceiling is way up there, but the game is also relaxing to play casually. Dustforce's mechanics are a fairly unique form of movement to traditional platformers, so the basics may feel clunky at first as you try to understand how to use your abilities efficiently. If you've played Melee, Dustforce will be no stranger to you.
If you're worried about the game's difficulty, there are bountiful community resources to help you improve. Even if you're not the competitive type, learning the mechanics will make the game much more interesting to navigate beyond the bouncy music and cheery visuals, plus it'll cut down on frustration trying to SS the later levels.
Completionists and speedrunners will get the most out of this game. Exploration is awarded with secrets hidden in nearly every level, and the community loves healthy competition in the leaderboards.
After 400 hours of (online and offline) play, there's a reason Dustforce is my favourite game of all time.

So, after finishing the first one in the series, I was more than eager to see just what Rapture had in store for me. The excitement of being a big daddy, not only for show, like the first title, but an actual living, breathing big daddy... was nothing like I expected.
A game's job is to convey the intended experience to the player, and every aspect of it must reinforce the suspension of disbelief, and immerse the player into the game world. In The Witcher, you feel like a mighty, skilled demon slayer, that is however, still a human and a mortal; in Darkest Dungeon you feel helpless, and fearful, even when fully geared and learned, you fear every step could be your last. So it's only natural to expect that being a Big Daddy, a bio-engineered living weapon, created solely to protect little sisters against any and all threats, would feel big, and imposing, and mighty... nothing further from the truth.
Once under the big daddy's helmet, you don't feel large, or powerful and, if anything, you feel weaker than a stranded survivor with a wrench. The iconic drill, so powerful it could pin a splicer against the wall, and shatter bulletproof glass, feels like a gimicky low power, fuel hungry tickle machine. The mighty rivet gun barely makes a dent on the splicers and machines, your melee hits annoy the splicers, instead of pushing them back against the wall, and overall, you feel like a random dumbass inside a diver's suit, not like a mighty engine of destruction, hellbent in settling matters.
I failed the check for suspension of disbelief one too many times on this one, and lost interest to play a big daddy, if said big daddy can be taken down with 3 gunshots from a random splicer, as opposed to the powerful behemoths that took an RPG to the face, and rammed you against the wall in retaliation. Minor notes were the now dumbified hacking process, the lack of variety in... everything, but what lost me was the ridiculous nerfing of the Big Daddy.

I picked this one up during the free weekend and was hooked instantly. As an Analyst in my day job and a “numbers guy” in general, I am thoroughly enjoying this one. It’s a very well balanced casual, play at your own pace, build your own fate with what your dealt, typical card based game. At 11 hours of playtime, I’m almost through the third world. At this point, I can’t tell how many worlds there are (based on the size of the board I’m assuming 4), but the worlds consist of 5 or 6 levels and within those levels are 1 to 3 missions with different objectives.
 
Every time you start a dungeon, your character starts from level one. This forces you to fight more enemies in a single mission to level up your character and stack your deck with better cards. You have numerous deck enhancements and new character decks that are available for upgrade that you can earn between missions.  I hear a lot of complaining that the game is “luck based”. Some aspects are but in general this is not true, if you analyze your enemy/objectives, you can easily figure out statically which deck will work best to beat the level. Yes, the method does require some trial and error and sometimes it does come down to the luck of the draw but that need for luck can be minimized if you know your character decks. Besides, anyone who’s been to Vegas or did a little gambling knows that half the fun is in the luck of the draw!
 
There were a couple of things that upset me about this game, but the more I play it and get used to the mechanics, these issues became less of an issues and made a little more sense to me. Like the Dungeoneer movement. You have little control of where the character moves and there are times when important to get your Dungeoneer to certain space on the board within a certain amount of moves. IMO this is where the game really comes down to the luck of the draw as there are no upgrades that affect your corridor pieces, fountain pieces, loot pieces, or enemy pieces. If you do not draw the dungeon building cards you need, you are screwed! My other gripe is that I wish the characters, enemies, and fountains specific effects were more visible. As of this current version, you have to hover over the effect names, cards, characters and enemies, just to figure out what is going to do what! I dunno, maybe just part of the challenge...
 
In all, considering the earworms and little gripes (-2), I’d give this a solid 8/10 for its insanely addicting gameplay and challenges. Guild of Dungeoneering is absolute nostalgia for any fan of DnD, Magic, or Hero's Quest! On the other hand, if you are not into the casual, card based, boardgame RPG type gameplay, this is one you should avoid!!

To make it worse, your adventurers' equipment and level is reset if they survive the dungeon and you lose the adventurer (to be replaced with a fresh new one) if they die. So, ultimately, there's no real powering. Your tier one adventurers only have a 50/50 change in the tier one dungeons and no chance in the tier two dungeons. I'm sorry, I can't even bring myself to properly review this. I just can't stand playing it anymore. Confrontation is supposed to be a Tactical RPG. However, there are huge problems with both the Tactics, and the RPG. It just seems very rushed and unpolished.
I'll only write about 2 general points: Story and Combat.
Regarding the Story, this game seems to have a huge lore. That lore is, of course, necessary to understand what's happening. However, they decided to give you access to it through pages and pages of text in the menu... I doubt anyone will read those out of nowhere. It's clearly for the people already familiar with the universe.
Besides, all the exposition is through narrated walls of texts. It's just like getting a few pages of an audiobook between each mission. It's completely separated from the game itself.
Now, about the Combat. First off, it's clunky as hell. I've played a few tactical games like this before. The fact that this game is in Real-Time rather than Turn-Based only hurts it. I've played Krater, though, and however flawed, that game feels good to play. Where this fails is that it's completely unresponsive, in the literal sense of the word. You command your character to do something, and they generally just ignore it. Either that, or they take
. After those seconds, someone important has already died, so tough luck.
The abilities also have long cooldowns, meaning you'll only be able to use them one -- twice at most -- per encounter.
The level design is also just a corridor with combat after combat. Sometimes you'll have to press levers, but that's about it.
Maybe I'm not giving it a fair enough chance and it gets better later on. After 6 hours, however, it feels just like I'm starting with it, and the game has done nothing interesting... and I can withstand not interesting, as long as it still feels good to play. With the clunky mechanics at play here, though, I won't.

I've devoted over 500 hours to this game over the last 3 years and I don't regret it at all. With such a massive amount of things to accomplish it almost never ends. From pvp to quests to farming with your friends to just goofing around and trying out new builds, the game is super fun. I thought I'd give my honest opinion on the game and why I think it's one of the best mmo's out there today.
Pros:
The story has come so far and is very immersive. Very rich lore. However if you don't pay attention to what's going on around you you'll be very lost. A lot of the story isn't told directly and has to be told through quests and paying attention to the world around you. For example, how the different factions interact with each other and what their goals are, is explained through doing missions and putting together puzzle pieces by listening to what the NPCs say.
This is a farming and hard♥♥♥♥♥grinding game. If you don't like the grind for better upgrades, parts for weapons or certain drops/events then perhaps this isn't the one for you. Although the payoff feels so good when you finally get the item you were farming so hard to get and now you get to craft your item and show it off to your friends. A wide arsenal of weapons and gear you can pick from leads to an unlimited possibility of builds, along with customizable mods to add to your weapons and warframes in order to make them fit your play style, make them stronger and more efficient. Making everyone you meet along the way unique from everyone else. Oh, did I mention that every weapon and Warframe can be acquired for FREE!
That brings me to my next point where this game is absolutely 100% free to play. The only thing you must pay real money for is cosmetics, which you'd only get if you really wanna look cool (Hence the nickname for the game "FashionFrame") or want to support it. Everything in the game can be acquired and there is no p2p aspect to it at all. No monthly subscriptions. No secret p2w shortcut (Although if you do pay a hefty amount of money you can aquire things very quickly. But what's the fun in that?) and no DLC's. Screw that. Everything can be acquired with a bit of farming. The real money ingame currency is called Platinum and can be traded with other players for parts for weapons and such. This gives the game an entire thriving economy. Don't have any platinum? Farm for parts and items people are looking for and are to lazy to get themselves and sell them. That's how I earn my platinum. Platinum can be used to buy almost everything in game from weapons and warframes to cosmetics. Although I save my platinum for specific items that the ingame market does not offer that people are selling in game.
The community is amazing in this game. When I first started out I had no idea what I was doing. I did a public mission and met a guy who was so far into the game. He saw I was new and asked if I had any questions. So I asked away and got familiar with the game very quickly as he showed me around and helped me acquire my first new warframe. Out of my entire time playing I've never seen one toxic or negative person. Everyone just wants to help each other and have fun. Best gaming community out there if you ask me. And joining a clan will help you by not only finding a few more friends along the way but getting your hands on some new gear only acquired by being in a clan, which are very easy to join. You'll grow a very strong pride for your clan and alliance which gives a competitive feel for when your clan goes to conqour dark sectors, which are areas that are controlled by clans. As for the development team they are very interactive with the players. Answering questions and listening to the players ideas and thoughts while responding with real care and interest. They are very indulged with their game and the players love DE as well <3
The graphics are stunning and utterly remarkable. I have a pretty crappy computer setup yet I manage to run the game smoothly on medium setting and it looks awesome. I can only imagine how it looks at high. The color scheme to the art style is perfectly fitting and almost feels realistic at times or something straight out of star wars. Nothing is half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥or seemed to be created in a lazy fashion. The detail and creativity that went into the development of this game really shows. The gameplay is very smooth as well and very simple. Some of the jump techniques might be a little tricky at first but can be easily mastered with a bit of practice. It has all the aspects of a shooter game and the aspects of a melee game such as parry, heavy hits, light hits and combos to slaughter your enemies with. It always feel good to see your enemies littered with bullet holes or to see them vaporize or get sliced up into little pieces. The UI is kept simple and easy to read along with the other utilities in the game like the arsenal menu and the foundry (Where you can make new items for yourself)
Now here come my cons:
The game is very unique in so many ways and has come a very long way to get where it is today and I honestly think it is one of, if not the best, mmorpg game that's completely f2p. But the only thing that is not unique is the tilemaps. The maps in this game start to get very old after awhile of playing them. Although as you progress through the game you get to go to different tilemaps but they all tend to get old eventually. They're recycled and reused. If you're doing a mission on venus on land and you go to another mission on venus on land they will be exactly the same tilemap. Although they do spawn you in different areas on the map every time and the maps are fairly big so atleast you get to enjoy them a bit more before you start to figure out where everything is. The enemies are kind of the same way too. As they are reused fairly often. They can also be a bit clunky at times. But I think that adds a bit of humor to the game.
After acquiring most of your wants and needs in the game after the countless hours of grinding and researching the game starts to lose its drive. Since there's nothing more you want, why keep playing? This has happened to me on multiple occasions. And updates for the game tend to come out every month or so, which add tons of new gear and a new quest and frame to farm which always brings me to play again and see what's new. The game is constantly being improved and can be played forever if you'd like.
Not sure if I should consider this a con or not but I'm gonna put it in here anyway as some people might think it is. When I first introduced the game to my friends they all thought it was just another shoot em up game with no skill(Even though it is technically a shoot em up game), as they tend to see me mashing my keyboard and coming out on top. I explain to them that at lower levels enemies are super easy to kill. It's just to make it easier and make it more appealing to beginners so they're not discouraged or get frustrated at hard enemies. As you progress the enemies get immensely harder and more challenging, making strategy key. Some might be turned off by the game not being challenging at first is the point I am trying to make.
Warframe is always improving and is always adding new elements to the game. If you're looking for a new game to spend hours in and get lost in its rich gameplay and community then this is the game for you. As long as you don't mind the grind it's an amazing game to immerse yourself in and meet awesome people. I highly recommend this game to anyone or to at least try it out. A big 10/10 for me. Thank you DE for such a fantastic game that I will continue playing for only Lotus knows how long.

Almost to 100 hours now, so I feel it's time for a review. I'm hooked on this game and Plains of Eidolon hasn't even released yet. I'm going to go over how Warframe handles the 3 core pillars to an RPG experience: Mechanics, Progression, and Customization. Then I'll talk about the business model.
Mechanics - Warframe has fun mechanics. The shooting feels good. Once you find some weapons you enjoy using the gunplay is as good as any shooter you'll find. The warframe abilities are fun to use once you get the hang of them. Melee combat is fun once you understand how stances, combos and channeling work. Where this game's mechanics really shine though is in its movement system. Not only is the movement speed fast, but once you master sliding, double jumping, wall climbing, rolling, and all of the movement "combos" you can pull off, the game offers more mobility than any shooter I've played.
Progression - Warframe has one of the most complicated progression systems I've ever seen in a game. You craft weapons and warframes, then level them up. The higher level they get, the more mods you can put in them. The mods give a variety of buffs and offer a wide variety of ways to build your weapons and warframes to suit your playstyle. You can get creative with them and completely change how certain weapons function. For example: I got a sniper rifle named Vectis Prime, to prepare for the Plains. Vectis is a semi-auto rifle with only a 2 shot magazine but fast reload speed. I got a mod that increases the damage of the first shot by 40%. Then I got a mod that reduces mag capacity but increases reload speed. So now it only holds one shot at a time, but with yet another mod that further increases reload speed, it reloads almost instantly. This makes it function more like a bolt-action rifle. On top of that there are flat damage boost mods, and elemental damage mods. You can combine different elements for new damage types, such as heat damage + poison damage = gas damage, which makes a cloud of AOE poison damage on impact. Really, this is all just scratching the surface of the complex yet rewarding progression system.
Customization - The customization options in Warframe are vast. For cosmetics, your Warframes and Weapons not only have skins you can obtain, but also seperate cosmetic armor pieces. You can also customize all the colors of your items. Then you can customize your playstyle through your choice of Warframes, guns and melee weapons. You have much more freedom to play with what suits you, because most of what determines how powerful a piece of gear is depends on the mods that were put in it. So even the weapons and warframes you get early in the game can be viable at end game, if you put good mods into them. You can also customize your spaceship, inside and out. Clans have huge customizable dojos. You can also choose a companion. These vary from small flying robots similar to Ghosts in the Destiny series, to space dogs and alien cats. There's even a mutant dog thing you can grow from a tumor that develops on your neck when you get infected by a virus that spreads through the player base.
Now, the elephant in the room. It's Free to Play, so there's a ton of Microtransactions. The premium currency, Platinum is kinda expensive, but here's something that's not discussed enough when it comes to this game's business model. TRADING. You can trade in-game items to other players for their premium currency. So, say you find a rare blueprint. You can go into trade chat, or one of the trading bazarres, find a whale with a bunch of platinum who wants to buy your blueprint, and boom, you now have the premium currency without spending a dime.
Awesome game, can't wait to see what Plains of Eidolon brings to the table.

When I discovered this game, i didn't expect it to have such great level design, tight controls, immense gameplay depth, amazing soundtrack and player freedom expression.
I also didn't expect it to be so hard.
This games follows in the shadow of other recent 2D platformers that makes their focus on beating tough as nails levels as fast as you can, like Super Meat Boy, Velocity or VVVVVV.
Personally I have always been drawn to games like this, ever since I first played Sonic the Hedgehog when I was just 4 years old.
As far as 2D platformers where the goal is to reach the finish line as fast as you can goes, this one stands out at the top of the list. It's no surprise, since the game clearly caters to the speedrunning community.
By that, I mean that it is possible to beat levels in less than a minute, without stoping or dealing with enemies, and the feeling is fantastic.
On the other hand, the game provides some moves that only expert players will learn because the game does not teach them to the players anywere in the game, but pulling it off in the long run makes you feel like a beast.
And that is my problem recommending it. It's definitely not a game for everyone.
Only the most persistent and skilled will reach the end of the game, and only a few dozens of players will beat the game 100%.
But for me that is the beauty of it. The game has no story, it expects you only to get good at the game, and the most positive thing, is that it feels outstanding getting good at the game.
Also, play it for the music alone. It's god tier

A creatively imagined multiplayer game. A surprisingly pleasant alternative to the brawler-type of multiplayer that has become so commonplace (e.g. samurai gunn, starwal, towerfall, bit-brawlers, brawlhalla, etc...), SpeedRunners offers players a spectrum of depth in gameplay. At its base, this game is a racing platformer, rewarding players who learn the turns and obstacles of various unique levels while punishing those who make mistakes. Perfectionism at its finest. This fine work does offer a deeper level of competition, however, if players chooses to exploit the nuances of the game's physics. With the mention of the glory of this game, I must also point out the negatives, which are frustratingly apparent within the first 5 minutes of gameplay. The matchmaking system is extremely unreliable, despite the implementation of a ranking system (albeit new). There are constant bugs in just about any multiplayer game, which would be endurable in a more forgiving game. The glitches can be brutal, and, due to the competitive nature of this game, they do not come off as humorous as in other games. At the rate at which this game has improved recently and with the massive community of stakeholders which it has garnered, SpeedRunners, while still in Beta at the moment of this review, will doubtlessly become one of the flawless go-to's for just about any friendly LAN party and competitive tournament. Each complaint I have for this game is tied to a problem that any early access game would have, and they are no reason to avoid a purchase. Currently an 8 / 10, this game is an easy pick-up and a difficult put-down!

SpeedRunners is a competitive racing game that is undeniably fun to play! The game is in beta at the time of this review, so I will note that there are bugs that exist in the game; these bugs are not game-breaking but you may find yourself a bit confused at times as to what's happening. The game has a very straightforward control system that can easily be learned. The learning curve to the game is relatively low, just about anyone can play it and have fun. One thing I was really impressed with, were the animations for the characters in SpeedRunners. There was a lot of detail put into every frame for the actors in the game. The stage design may be my only gripe with the game. I think all of the stages are fantastic, but there are some awkward placements of traps in the game that will make you question the purpose of its location. SpeedRunners doesnt have much of a story mode, its multiplayer aspect is where the game shines. So if you're looking for a game to play with a group of friends for some friendly trash-talking fun, I'd suggest buying SpeedRunners!

This is one of those games that may never recover from a horrible alpha that left a wake of bad reviews. That said, spite only one major glitch I've discovered in 24 hours of gameplay, this is easily on my top 3 favorite games.
EDIT: Ok, my OP was done from a phone; so lets crack this open.
This game is amazing, IDGAF what anyone says. But there are some experience breaking glitches that have yet to be resolved. They've released 2(?) "DLC" packs that contain additional maps to survive on. The problem is that I can't even bring myself to purchase these absolutely gorgeous maps, because;
#1 they're asking $30 which is half of the retail full price of the base game.
#2 is because owning the base game, I realized that I can hop onto a raptor and go for a swim, and next thing you know I'm entering a super sonic hyper speed that will launch me across the map if not careful (usually resulting in death of both myself and my raptor). I have seen other dinos with this hyper speed glich (spitters, carnos+). So why pay $30 for a "DLC" for a game that was never actually completed in the first place?
This game is FUN. Spite the bugs, I've enjoyed every minute of it. The developers gave the gamer complete control over server difficulty in that you control nearly every aspect of the servers mechanics. Vanilla settings are #missionimpossible. You'll spend hours training dinos, you'll die in 1 bite, you'll never recover your items because you'll die just trying to get to them. Thus, I recommend that if you do buy this game, you modify the server settings before starting. Did I mention vanilla settings mean it could take you hours to train a big dino?
I DO recommend this game to my friends. But I caution you that it is far from "perfect", but it is hands down the best survival game I've ever played. It's better than minecraft, better than rust, it's just F&(^(*^(*^ awesome.
Who wouldn't like taming dinosaurs and riding them across a huge world, exploring and gathering materials to develop massive fortresses? Insane people that's who!
As long as you don't exploit bugs (hyper swim speeds on certain mounts), you'll enjoy the experience if you're into survival. I usually just avoid the water and go the "long" route when riding raptors/other swim bugged mounts.
I don't do PvP so I cannot speak on the quality of experience. I hear that MP servers are horribly optimized, dealing with nasty rubberbanding (lots of lag). I play solo or host locally for my friends to play, and I have not had any issues.
I'll update this review after I get some more hours under the belt and experience the end game content.

Metro LL takes the 'bad ending' of Metro 2033 and continuing the story from there.
Continuing the journey of Artyom from Metro 2033, now he is a full fledged Spartan elite squad.
Artyom are now haunted by the action he took that kills an entire new race, or so he thought.
He is then tasked with eliminating a new threat that have just been founded, but upon seeing that this new threat is just a child of the Dark Ones that he just massacred, Artyom knew that he can maybe redeem himself.
Metro Last Light again delivers a single player experience just like Metro 2033, except with updated graphic quality.
The gameplay mechanic are still pretty much the same with the previous title.
After the main story, Metro LL offers other mode to play, supplied by the DLC (if you buy Metro LL redux, it comes with all DLC available). There are short story mission, involving a stealth sniper level and heavy combat of the fronline.
Also there are some background story mission -apart from the campaign- involving the major character in Last Light, playing this might give you more insight to those major character.
One of the DLC mission that shines the most is Kshatriya.
You are tasked as Kshatriya, a squad that retriev whatever useful item in the surface that can be recycled and used again by the Metro populace.
This mission gameplay is not quite the same with the campaign one, involving the player in a a true scavenging-survival mechanic.
Air filter is non-existent in the surface and so player must frequently back to base to restock and resupply. Player are given ingame money to purchase armory and survival gear if only they brought back artifact to be cashed in.
Coupled with radiation and enemy that lurks the environment, player must make flee-or-fight decision  in order to complete his task as Kshatriya
A discount purchase of this item, and you can net yourself some 30 hour-ish gametime.

SpeedRunners is a competitive racing game that is undeniably fun to play! The game is in beta at the time of this review, so I will note that there are bugs that exist in the game; these bugs are not game-breaking but you may find yourself a bit confused at times as to what's happening. The game has a very straightforward control system that can easily be learned. The learning curve to the game is relatively low, just about anyone can play it and have fun. One thing I was really impressed with, were the animations for the characters in SpeedRunners. There was a lot of detail put into every frame for the actors in the game. The stage design may be my only gripe with the game. I think all of the stages are fantastic, but there are some awkward placements of traps in the game that will make you question the purpose of its location. SpeedRunners doesnt have much of a story mode, its multiplayer aspect is where the game shines. So if you're looking for a game to play with a group of friends for some friendly trash-talking fun, I'd suggest buying SpeedRunners!

So apparently I'm just a bad guy when it comes to playing the metro games. This is the second time I've gotten the bad ending, which leaves me a bit confused. I get that there's a "moral points system" that judges how you do; and if you get enough points, you get the good ending; but still, there's something I'm not seeing here. This game gives you a lot of opportunities to do good things, and I did all of it. I gave money to the poor. I spared surrendering enemies. I listened to the end of a lot of conversations. I resisted getting revenge on some pretty terrible guys. I even helped little Timmy get his stuffed bear back... But I'm a bad guy. That just pets my goat.
Questionable video game moral systems aside; the rest of the game fares very well. Everything is polished; and this time around the story is cohesive and actually feels more appropriate. There's an actual antagonist in this story, which plays to its benefit very well. We also get to know a lot more about the world and the characters. And hey, our protagonist gets some exposition too! Woohoo! Improvements!
Gotta admit though, it feels pretty good to wield the fully automatic cheeky-breeky shotgun and absolutely blow people away. I have a feeling that if the guns weren't so interesting and fun to shoot, the game would've fallen pretty flat. The story can stand on its own, sure. Textures set the mood well enough; but the level design boils down to hallways. Lots of hallways. However, I managed to get around these problems and have a very enjoyable experience. There's just something charming about strolling around the dank metro, or the poisonous surface, and unloading on the first thing that wants to kill you.
A few more notes: Shoehorned romance sucks. Some of the particles are meh. I had to restart the last level because of a nasty crashing bug. A lot less motion blur this time around. The extra content feels lackluster after completing the main story, only good for an extra hour tops. Still a little mad about getting the bad ending.

When I entered the world of DOS 2 for the first time, I was instantly blown away by the graphics.  The new world is simply stunning, the artwork amazing and that alone made me instantly appreciate the game.  As I played a couple of the characters, I recognized that each of them have some sort of flaw, past, something unknown driving them and a big part of the game is me figuring what that is and it is going to lead to a great story. That and of course some great, challenging battles.
One thing I knew instantly though, I wanted that damn collar off.
There is familiarity, much of the crafting is the same with many new ones.  So are a few of the spells, but they act a little differently. I wondered how they would come up with spells that are more fun than the original, but they did it. One item I absolutely LOVE in this game is the bedroll.  That one thing alone is a huge timesaver after a battle as in DOS it would take me time to apply all of the various heals to get my characters up again if there were no beds about.  I do hope they will come up with something for repairs so that in game I don't have to spend so much time repairing every single slot on the character page.
So do I recommend this game? Hell, yes.  However, it is alpha so think of it as a preview of what I think could become the game of the year for 2017. (No pressure Devs)  It will be some time before you can get to the end game on this one.  If that will frustrate you, I would say wait.  BUT, if you want to alpha test and watch a game develop as you play you HAVE to go ahead and buy this one, you are going to want to when it is fully released anyway.

SpeedRunners is an action platformer that pits you against your opponents in a 4 player race! The aim of the game is to outrun your opponents by forcing them to fall off-screen. There are also items, switches and a few other mechanics that assist in your run. There are various different maps to choose from, including a level editor that allows people to share and play custom levels.
Let's start with the gameplay. SpeedRunners is very enjoyable to play, especially with a group of friends. You'll be racing each other for hours; running, dashing, sliding, grapling, and whatever you can do to retain your lead position. Although it is fun, the gameplay is a little bit repetitive with the same goal all the time. However, the level editor does nullify some of this repetitiveness, as well as the random wheel thing that rarely spawns and altars gameplay for that round.
In terms of graphics, this is the main area where the game is being let down the most. The textures themselves are a solid effort, but the particle systems are lacking a lot. The game could use some more particle effects to polish it. Yes, it is still in Beta, and polishing is usually left till last, but it is still valid for the current version. I do hope they improve this when the game is out of Beta.
Overall, a solid effort still in the works. I hope to see something spectatular with this when it is out of Beta. I cannot write a full review just yet, and the rating will have to wait.

What a great addition to the platformer genre. Dustforce is an indie action platformer from Hitbox Team. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
I love platformers and Dustforce made me remember why I love platformers. Everything about this game is well done and polished until it shines.
First thing first, you’ll be hard pressed to find another game with as good a soundtrack as the one that accompanies Dustforce. It is pure, relaxing majesty and nothing could possibly fit this game better in terms of music. It makes you feel good while you play.
The art is phenomenal. Character designs are simple and beautiful, enemies are original, and the environments themselves will provide you with a good eyeful as well.
The controls are smooth and fluid. You can easily transition from floors to ceilings in a matter of seconds, all the while cleaning the living hell out of dust ridden creatures and persons. Dustforce is, essentially, 2D parkour and I love it.
There are a huge amount of levels for you to play through with four different characters, all of whom have their own play style. Not only does the core game have over 100 levels, but there are a heaping amount of user created levels that you can play through as well. The fun doesn’t have to end with this one, ever.
The Bad
Nothing. Nothing at all my friends.
The Meh
See the above category, please.
Verdict: Yea
Dustforce is a lighthearted, refreshing platformer that serious and casual gamers alike can enjoy at their leisure. If you’re looking for something new to play, look no further. As always, thanks for reading.
